dimensions.title: Backend architecture & code quality
dimensions.summary: The backend is a mature, thoughtfully-engineered codebase: leaf packages (atomic.py, runner.py, derive.py/OffsetMap, tracks/registry.py) are cohesive, fail-loud, and correct, with rich docstrings that record the reasoning behind past bug fixes. The dominant structural weakness is server.py: a 2989-LOC module whose create_app is a single ~2150-line function holding all 77 endpoints as closures, and — critically — the one place in the codebase that bypasses atomic.py. Every track/CLI/runner path writes atomically, but server.py (0 atomic references) and derive.py/layout.py's save_layout truncate-in-place on load-bearing files (layout_sections.json, annotation tracks, character cache, alignment metadata), reintroducing the exact C3 torn-read and C1 missing-provenance classes the atomic/runner refactors were built to eliminate. The KJV verse-paragraph fix is verified correct and reflected end-to-end (1071==1071 on disk; clean full-length diagonal in the dotplot viz).
strengths: atomic.py is textbook-correct: temp-file-in-same-dir + f.flush() + os.fsync() + os.replace(), with BaseException cleanup of the temp file (atomic.py:22-39). runner.py, cli.py, and all 8 track modules consistently route writes through it.

runner.py is a model of separation-of-concerns: it exists specifically to share the masked-run path between HTTP and CLI (runner.py:4-9), has no web-framework dependency so the CLI imports it without FastAPI, and _remap_signal_dir fails LOUD via UnmappedCoordinateError rather than writing analyzable coords mislabeled as original (runner.py:39-43).

OffsetMap (derive.py:33-142) enforces its ordered/disjoint/non-empty precondition at construction with ValueError (derive.py:60-67) instead of silently mistranslating, uses bisect for O(log n) on 10^5 records, documents and honors the inverse_point(translate_point(x))==x round-trip invariant, and correctly distinguishes inverse_element (single-span, exact) from inverse_span (bridges excised gaps).

The module-scope request-BaseModel gotcha is honored AND documented as a warning to future editors: AlignmentRequest/LiftoverRequest/ProbeRequest/SweepRequest all sit at module scope with explicit comments explaining that from __future__ import annotations + get_type_hints would silently degrade a function-local model to a query param (server.py:129-133,140-142,151-155,170-174).

tracks/registry.py dependency_order uses Kahn's algorithm with explicit cycle detection (raises ValueError naming the offending tracks, registry.py:81-83) and duplicate-name detection (registry.py:31-35); tracks/base.py is a clean runtime-checkable Protocol enabling structural subtyping with no forced inheritance.

The KJV paragraph fix is verified true end-to-end: on disk all six members now have paras==verses (KJV Matthew 1071==1071, KJV Mark 678==678, Geneva 1071, DR-Matthew 1070 Vulgate versification), and the GEN-Mt vs KJV-Mt dotplot renders one clean sharp full-length 1071x1071 diagonal (screenshot 07-compare-dotplot.png), the exact ground-truth signal the collection is designed to exercise.

findings.title: save_layout writes layout_sections.json non-atomically, and load_layout triggers that rewrite on a read path
findings.evidence: layout.py:307-310 (save_layout uses raw .write_text); layout.py:289-304 (load_layout calls save_layout to backfill parents during a READ)
findings.recommendation: Route save_layout through atomic_write_text. layout_sections.json defines every project's structure/masking; a truncate-in-place rewrite torn by process death or observed mid-write by a concurrent reader (the analysis-status poller, or any parallel request loading the same project) yields a JSON parse error that makes the whole project appear corrupt. That load_layout rewrites it as a side effect of reading amplifies the concurrency window. This is precisely the C3 scenario atomic.py exists to prevent, in the most load-bearing file.
findings.verify_reasoning: Grounded in the cited code and the atomic infrastructure. save_layout (layout.py:307-310) uses raw Path.write_text (truncate-in-place, non-atomic). load_layout (layout.py:289-304) calls save_layout as a side effect of a READ, to backfill parent_id on legacy layouts (parents_computed=False), catching only OSError. This is a genuine read-path write. The concurrency claim holds: load_layout runs on hot read paths — GET /api/projects/{id}/sections offloads it to a worker thread (server.py:2109-2123), and it is also invoked from project.py:303 (masked_intervals, used by every analysis extractor), server.py:377 (chunk-layer stats), derive.py:515, and integrity.py:65. Concurrent GETs on the same not-yet-backfilled project would each attempt a rewrite, and any reader reading the file bytes during the write can observe a truncated/partial JSON that json.loads fails on, making the project appear corrupt. The codebase's own atomic.py docstring explicitly names this exact scenario ("A concurrent reader ... reading a manifest while a job rewrites it, finding C3, can then observe half a file") and provides atomic_write_text (temp file + fsync + os.replace); every other JSON writer routes through it (runner.py, cli.py, signals.py, all tracks/*.py, annotation/serializer.py, write_run_provenance). save_layout is the sole exception, and it writes the single most load-bearing per-project file (defines structure + masking for all downstream analysis). The recommendation (route save_layout through atomic_write_text) is correct and one line. Two fair mitigations that bound but do not refute: (1) the backfill amplifier is one-time-per-project — parents_computed is persisted and idempotent (verified in test_layout.py:128-146 and layout.py:299), so after first successful backfill reads no longer write; the perpetual read-write framing is slightly overstated. (2) A torn read requires a reader hitting the microsecond write window or a process death mid-write, so realized frequency is low. Still, the defect is real, sits on the most critical file, and contradicts the project's own established C3 guardrail — I did not trigger the live write to avoid violating READ-ONLY, but the code path is unambiguous. High severity is warranted.

findings.title: server.py never imports atomic.py — 6 non-atomic writes to files that are concurrently read
findings.evidence: grep -c atomic server.py == 0; non-atomic write_text at server.py:436 (_remap_tracks_dir rewrites annotation .jsonl), :562/:1919 (manifests), :597 (verses.jsonl), :1079/:1102 (characters.json), :2772 (alignment metadata.json). Contrast atomic write_track at annotation/serializer.py:36-41.
findings.recommendation: Import atomic_write_text and use it for all six. The character-cache case is a concrete race: get_characters (server.py:1069) and get_cooccurrence (server.py:1092) both read cache/characters.json while both write it non-atomically (server.py:1079,1102) on a cache miss; concurrent first-requests can read a torn file. metadata.json at :2772 is read by alignment_status to report record_count — a torn read reports a garbage count.
findings.verify_reasoning: I verified every code location cited. CONFIRMED: grep -c "atomic" core/palimpsest/server.py == 0 and there is no `atomic` import; all cited non-atomic Path.write_text sites exist exactly as described — :436 (_remap_tracks_dir rewriting annotation .jsonl), :562 and :1919 (manifests), :597 (verses.jsonl), :1079 and :1102 (cache/characters.json), :2772 (comp_dir/metadata.json). The contrast is real and damning: annotation/serializer.py:41 write_track uses atomic_write_text, and its own docstring (lines 36-37) explicitly cites finding C3 ("a torn .jsonl ... a concurrent reader mid-write"). So the atomic-write pattern already exists to fix precisely this bug class, yet these server.py sites were left non-atomic — a genuine, self-inconsistent gap. The headline "concrete race" is confirmed verbatim: get_characters (read :1069, write :1079) and get_cooccurrence (read :1092, write :1102) are two independent async GET endpoints that both read and non-atomically write cache/characters.json on a cache miss, with no lock (server has only asyncio.Semaphore(3), which limits but does not serialize file access); concurrent first-requests can observe a torn file. I also confirmed the annotation tracks rewritten non-atomically at :436 during a batch run (called from :1925) are servable over HTTP via serve_project_file FileResponse (:2962), so a real concurrent reader exists. REFUTED DETAIL: the auditor's specific claim that "metadata.json at :2772 is read by alignment_status to report record_count" is false — alignment_status (:2792-2802) reads the in-memory _alignment_jobs dict and, in the fallback path, only checks for alignment.jsonl existence, returning {"status":"completed"} with NO record_count; it never opens metadata.json. HOWEVER a real reader of comp_dir/metadata.json does exist at collections_masking.py:_find_pair (:316-317), used during liftover, where a torn read raises an uncaught json.JSONDecodeError — so the underlying "metadata.json has a torn-read-vulnerable reader" concern still holds, just via the wrong-named reader. Net: the finding is real and well-grounded; one supporting example is misattributed but a valid substitute exists. SEVERITY: I lower high→medium. Impact is real but bounded — the affected files (character cache, manifests, verses track, metadata) are regenerable/reproducible; a torn read surfaces as a JSONDecodeError/500 or a parse error, not silent persistent corruption; and the race windows are narrow (only on first cache miss / during a batch-run remap). It is a correctness bug worth fixing (import atomic_write_text at the seven sites), but not a high-severity data-integrity or security issue.

findings.title: collection_probe and collection_sweep run CPU/IO-heavy work synchronously on the event loop
findings.evidence: server.py:2510 probe_corpus(...) and server.py:2534 sweep_pairwise(...) called directly in async handlers with no asyncio.to_thread; both are plain sync functions with per-member vector loops (collections_probe.py:141 probe_corpus, collections_sweep.py:140 sweep_pairwise, the latter documented as pruning an O(N*M) chunk-pair space).
findings.recommendation: Wrap both calls in await asyncio.to_thread(...), matching the alignment/embedding/character endpoints which all offload correctly (server.py:1076,1306,2743-2768). As written, a single sweep/probe over the 6-way corpus blocks all other requests (status polls, the UI) for its entire duration.

findings.title: Alignment and embedding background jobs bypass the _job_semaphore that is supposed to bound O(n^2) work
findings.evidence: server.py:24-25 defines _job_semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(3) 'to prevent saturation on O(n^2) workloads'; only the track-analyze run() acquires it (server.py:1305 async with _job_semaphore). run_alignment's run() (server.py:2726) and the embeddings run() (server.py:1556) never acquire it, yet alignment invokes compute_cross_similarity (a full O(n^2) matrix).
findings.recommendation: Acquire _job_semaphore inside the alignment and embedding background tasks too, or document why they are exempt. Firing alignment for many corpus pairs currently spawns unbounded concurrent to_thread computations, defeating the semaphore's stated purpose.

findings.title: create_app is a ~2150-line god-function holding all 77 endpoints as closures; three duplicated ad-hoc job-tracking systems
findings.evidence: server.py:835 def create_app ... server.py:2981 return app (endpoints grep -cE '@app.(get|post|delete|put)' == 77, all nested); three separate in-memory job dicts each with hand-rolled create_task + call_later cleanup: _running_jobs (server.py:1109), _alignment_jobs (server.py:2703), and import tasks (server.py:2072,2264).
findings.recommendation: Split routers by domain (projects, collections, alignment, corpus) via APIRouter, and unify the three job dicts behind one small job-registry abstraction. Beyond maintainability: job state lives in process-local closures, so it is lost on restart and is wrong under any multi-worker uvicorn deployment (a status poll can hit a worker that never ran the job).

findings.title: Batch import path re-implements track persistence inline, skipping run-provenance (reintroduces finding C1)
findings.evidence: Single-track path uses shared runner helpers: extract_masked + persist_track_outputs (server.py:1306-1311), which writes manifest atomically AND write_run_provenance (runner.py:118-127). Batch _compute_tracks writes manifest with non-atomic .write_text (server.py:1919-1920) and calls no write_run_provenance at all.
findings.recommendation: After the batch view is remapped, emit run-provenance per track (and use atomic_write_text for the manifest). As-is, batch-imported projects have manifests/*.manifest.json but no *.run.json, while single-track-analyzed projects have both — so _track_run_info (server.py:203) silently shows no clamp/provenance for batch-imported tracks, the exact 'one entry point lacks a param record' bug atomic.write_run_provenance was created to close.

findings.title: derive.py _write_jsonl writes derived subtext tracks non-atomically
findings.evidence: derive.py:427-431 (_write_jsonl uses raw path.write_text); this rewrites derived subtext annotation .jsonl tracks during derive_subtext, while the canonical write_track (annotation/serializer.py:38-41) is atomic.
findings.recommendation: Route _write_jsonl through atomic_write_text for consistency with write_track and the rest of the derive/runner pipeline. Derivation is exactly when many track files are (re)written in sequence; a crash mid-derive leaves a torn subtext track that later fails to parse.

findings.title: /api/search and /api/explain reimplement the path-traversal guard inline instead of calling _safe_project_dir
findings.evidence: _safe_project_dir (server.py:631-640) is the belt-and-suspenders guard (string check + resolve + is_relative_to + is_dir). server.py:1007-1011 duplicates that logic inline for GET /api/search (a raw project: str query param with no pydantic pattern). server.py:909-910 for POST /api/explain only checks '..' in request.project (the real protection is the model's Field pattern at server.py:60).
findings.recommendation: Have both endpoints call _safe_project_dir. Copy-pasting security-critical traversal logic invites drift (the /api/explain variant is already weaker than the helper, saved only by the incidental pydantic pattern); centralizing it removes the divergence risk entirely.

findings.title: TrackRegistry.discover silently drops any track module that fails to import
findings.evidence: registry.py:97-100 and 109-112 catch ImportError and only logger.warning('Skipping track module ...'); a failed import (e.g. embedding_track needing numpy/sqlite_vec) removes that track from the registry with no runtime error.
findings.recommendation: Consider fail-loud (or at least surfacing a machine-readable 'unavailable tracks' list in the analysis-status payload) for core tracks. As written, a broken dependency makes a track silently vanish from every analysis run — the kind of silent degradation the codebase elsewhere explicitly rejects (cf. runner.py's UnmappedCoordinateError fail-loud philosophy).

findings.title: _load_spacy_model silently falls back to en_core_web_sm on load failure
findings.evidence: project.py:48-56: on OSError loading the requested model it substitutes spacy.load('en_core_web_sm') with no record; entities/coreference/syntax outputs would then differ from the requested model with no on-disk or API trace.
findings.recommendation: Record the actually-loaded model in the track's provenance/meta (as lithmm already does for its KMeans fallback, surfaced via _track_run_info at server.py:236-246), so a downgraded NLP run is visible to the user rather than a hidden fallback (a documented anti-pattern: 'Fallbacks Are Failures').

dimensions.title: API contract & endpoint integrity
dimensions.summary: The ~77-endpoint FastAPI surface (core/palimpsest/server.py) is well-structured with disciplined path-traversal guards, mostly-consistent 400/404 error codes, and self-describing binary/JSON matrix manifests, and the recent verse-paragraphing fix genuinely holds (KJV members now 1071/678 verses; the Geneva-Matt vs KJV-Matt dotplot shows one clean full-length 1071x1071 diagonal; corpus graph = 1 core/1 shell/6 singleton; phyletic tree roots DR). HOWEVER the codebase carries a systemic split between two embedding-DB path conventions: the canonical EmbeddingTrack writes cache/embeddings_{label}.db, but the alignment engine, embeddings/status, embeddings/compute, search and CLI-analyze all hardcode the legacy unlabeled cache/embeddings.db. On the live 6-way collection this makes the app's own default semantic alignment path unreachable and makes embeddings/status directly contradict the congruence badge for the same member. As a result every stored comparison, sweep, corpus graph and phyletic tree is built purely from word_overlap edges — the cosine/embedding ground-truth signal the collection was designed to exercise is never actually computed through the app.
strengths: Path-traversal + id validation is consistent and correct: _safe_project_dir (server.py:631-640) returns 400 on ../ or slash and 404 on missing project; _validate_ids / _ID_PATTERN (server.py:2706-2710) enforce ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$ and return 400 on malformed ids (live: /api/alignment/bad..id/other/records -> 400).

Congruence contract is principled and correct: congruence_report (collections_ops.py:242-283) folds the embedding model_fingerprint into the comparability key; live cosine probe on the 6-way returns all_congruent=true, missing=[], one shared key embedding:cosine:c9757c16f8473ef1 across all 6 members, and word_overlap returns needs_embedding=false with tokens:word_overlap — the fix (all 6 embedded, cosine-congruent) verifiably holds at the congruence layer.

Binary matrix contracts are self-describing where it matters: /matrix JSON manifest declares dimensions:[1071,678], dtype:float32, byte_order:little-endian, and the matrix.bin content-length (2,904,552 = 1071x678x4) matches exactly; embedding heatmap endpoint emits X-Matrix-N / X-Matrix-Reduced / X-Matrix-Order headers (server.py:1686-1691).

The verse-paragraphing fix is confirmed end-to-end: KJV cross_similarity manifests carry the correct 1071/678 verse dimensions, screenshot 07-compare-dotplot.png shows the near-identical Geneva-Matt vs KJV-Matt pair as one clean full-length diagonal, and the corpus graph summary is exactly the designed pangenome (core:1, shell:1, singleton:6) with the phyletic tree rooting DR (DRMt suggested_root).

Query-parameter validation on analytical endpoints is thorough: projection rejects non-pca with 400 (server.py:1624), distances rejects bad kind with 400 (1641), lane/heatmap validate encoding/order (1673,1719), and Query(...ge=/le=) bounds are applied consistently to bins/k/window/limit.

findings.title: Embedding-DB path split makes the default semantic-alignment path unreachable on embedded members
findings.evidence: core/palimpsest/alignment/cross_similarity.py:75 hardcodes emb_db = project.path/'cache'/'embeddings.db'; on disk every 6-way member has ONLY cache/embeddings_87da3afb...db (labeled), no unlabeled embeddings.db (verified: unlabeled_exists=NO for all 6). run_alignment (server.py:2756) calls compute_cross_similarity(...,'cosine') for method=semantic (the UI default), so it raises FileNotFoundError('Embeddings not found... Run palimpsest analyze') despite the member being embedded.
findings.recommendation: Resolve the embedding DB via the same newest-wins/labeled logic used by member_embedding_layer / _embedding_db_path (cache/embeddings_{label}.db) inside compute_cross_similarity._load_embeddings, or pass the resolved label from run_alignment. Add a regression test that runs method=semantic against a labeled-DB member.
findings.verify_reasoning: Verified end-to-end. (1) CODE: core/palimpsest/alignment/cross_similarity.py:75 hardcodes emb_db = project.path/'cache'/'embeddings.db' and raises FileNotFoundError('Embeddings not found... Run `palimpsest analyze`') at :77-80. (2) ROUTING: server.py run_alignment (:2755-2756) sends method=semantic (the else/non-alphabet/non-word branch) into compute_cross_similarity(proj_a, proj_b, 'cosine') -> _load_embeddings. AlignmentRequest.method defaults to 'semantic' (server.py:137) and the frontend comparisonStore.ts:81 sets activeMethod:'semantic' as default, POSTing to /api/alignment/run (comparisonStore.ts:100-103). (3) DISK: for all 6 project_ids returned by GET /api/collections (matthew-mark-6way), every leaf member has ONLY a labeled embeddings_{hash}.db (e.g. KJV-Matthew embeddings_87da3afb423732be.db) and unlabeled_exists=NO — matches the finding exactly. (4) RUNTIME: I reproduced FileNotFoundError by calling _load_embeddings via core/.venv on the real KJV-Matthew member; it raised the exact misleading 'Run palimpsest analyze' message despite the member being MLX-embedded. (5) ROOT CAUSE: the current pipeline EmbeddingTrack._embed (embedding_track.py:129) writes ONLY embeddings_{label}.db; grep shows the unlabeled embeddings.db is written solely by the LEGACY /api/projects/{id}/embeddings/compute path (server.py:1519,1559) and cli.py — not by the layer/collections flow used to build these members. The frontend even documents the split (AnalysisPanel.tsx:475: 'legacy paragraph-embedding cache /embeddings/compute -> cache/embeddings.db'). So a member embedded via the modern/collections path is unreachable by the default semantic pairwise alignment. The recommended fix is sound and consistent with existing code: member_embedding_layer (collections_ops.py:217) already implements the newest-wins/labeled resolution, and server._embedding_db_path (:282-294) already resolves embeddings_{label}.db. SEVERITY: adjusted critical->high. It breaks the UI-default alignment mode for members produced by the standard pipeline with a misleading error, but a functional (if non-obvious, cross-panel) workaround exists — the legacy /embeddings/compute endpoint + AnalysisPanel 'Compute Embeddings' dialog can populate the unlabeled DB, after which semantic alignment works; and the AlignmentView itself offers no in-place remediation. Not fully unreachable in the absolute sense, hence high rather than critical, but the bug and its user impact are real and confirmed.

findings.title: embeddings/status contradicts the congruence badge for the same member (two truth sources disagree)
findings.evidence: Live, same member (KJV-Matt): GET /api/projects/{id}/embeddings/status -> {"available":false,"count":0} (server.py:1490 reads legacy cache/embeddings.db) while GET /api/collections/matthew-mark-6way/congruence?metric=cosine -> all_congruent:true, missing:[] (reads labeled embeddings_{label}.db). Any UI gating the 'Align (Semantic)' button on embeddings/status sees no embeddings and blocks the operation the congruence badge advertises as ready.
findings.recommendation: Unify embeddings/status (server.py:1486-1501), embeddings/compute (1519), search (1015) and cli.py:146 onto the content-addressed embeddings_{label}.db resolver. embeddings/status should report the resolved label + count, matching the congruence view.
findings.verify_reasoning:
The underlying data-disagreement is REAL and I reproduced it live. For KJV-Matt (3rd member of matthew-mark-6way, id ...king-james...chapter-in-book-matthew), GET /api/projects/{id}/embeddings/status returns {"available":false,"count":0} while GET /api/collections/matthew-mark-6way/congruence?metric=cosine returns all_congruent:true, missing:[] with every member keyed embedding:cosine:c9757c16f8473ef1. Filesystem confirms why: server.py:1490 reads project_dir/cache/embeddings.db, and across all 6 members there are 0 legacy embeddings.db files but 8 labeled embeddings_{label}.db files (e.g. KJV-Matt has cache/embeddings_87da3afb423732be.db, 10MB, populated). congruence resolves labeled layers via _embedding_db_path/_enumerate_layers; embeddings/status, embeddings/compute (1519), search (1015) and cli.py:146 read the fixed legacy path. So the cited two-store split and the recommendation to unify the resolver are grounded and coherent.

However, the CRITICAL-severity RATIONALE is fabricated. The finding claims "Any UI gating the 'Align (Semantic)' button on embeddings/status sees no embeddings and blocks the operation." I grepped the entire frontend (browser/src): /api/projects/{id}/embeddings/status is referenced in EXACTLY ONE place — AnalysisPanel.tsx:532 (checkEmbeddings) — and it gates ONLY the legacy-cache tracks EMBEDDING_DEPENDENT_TRACKS={compartments,rqa,alphabet}. AnalysisPanel.tsx:476-478 explicitly documents that layer-consuming tracks (self_similarity) are DELIBERATELY excluded from this gate. The "Align (Semantic)" button lives in CompareView.tsx:169-175 (and CorpusView.tsx:358); it is disabled ONLY on `loading` and calls /api/alignment/run — it has NO reference to embeddings/status whatsoever. So no UI gates Align on embeddings/status; the claimed blocking mechanism does not exist. The captured screenshot .scratch/audit6/screenshots/07-compare-dotplot.png confirms this visually: Align is enabled (blue) and a 1071x1071 cross-similarity dotplot for Geneva-Matt vs KJV-Matt is rendered.

There is a genuinely-related but differently-scoped latent bug the finding did not correctly characterize: the semantic path of POST /api/alignment/run flows through compute_cross_similarity -> _load_embeddings (cross_similarity.py:75), which reads only the legacy cache/embeddings.db with no fallback to labeled layers, so a FRESH semantic Align on these members would raise FileNotFoundError. But that is a runtime failure of one endpoint, not the UI-gating/badge contradiction described, and it does not manifest here: all 16 stored .comparisons matrices are metric word_overlap (source word_overlap/0.1, text-only), and compute_cross_similarity has no caller besides alignment/run. In practice the collection is compared via the labeled-DB corpus-graph/word-overlap path, which works end-to-end (screenshots 02-* show masking/analyses/sweep/probe all rendering).

Net: real inconsistency between two embedding-store families (cosmetic/reporting + a latent semantic-alignment failure), but the impact is overstated — the specific "badge says ready, UI blocks the button" causal story is refuted by the code and the auditor's own screenshot. Downgrade critical -> low.

findings.title: Whole downstream stack (comparisons/sweep/corpus-graph/phyletic-tree) built only from word_overlap edges — the cosine ground-truth signal is never exercised
findings.evidence: GET /api/comparisons -> Counter({'word':16}); zero cosine/semantic comparisons exist. build_corpus_graph (corpus_graph.py:236) ingests whatever alignment.jsonl exists with no method filter, so the graph/pangenome/tree derive from word-overlap edges. The stored sweep is metric:word_overlap. This is a direct consequence of finding #1: because semantic alignment is broken, the collection's designed 'embeddings better for synoptic Mt<->Mk' signal has never been computed through the app.
findings.recommendation: After fixing #1, generate cosine comparisons for the 6-way and rebuild the graph; expose method as a corpus-graph/sweep parameter and record the edge method in provenance so word vs cosine derivations are distinguishable.
findings.verify_reasoning:
Every factual claim verified directly against the live API, on-disk artifacts, code, and screenshot.

1) Comparisons are all word: GET /api/comparisons -> 16 total, Counter({'word':16}); zero cosine/semantic. Corroborated on disk: all 16 metadata.json in .scratch/validation-mm/.comparisons/ report method 'word' (record_counts 0-103).

2) No method filter in graph build: corpus_graph.py:171 _find_comparison locates a comparison purely by (query_id,target_id) via comparison_dir with no method predicate; build_corpus_graph (corpus_graph.py:228-257) ingests whatever alignment.jsonl exists per pair. Confirmed.

3) Downstream derives from word edges: stored corpus_graph.json for matthew-mark-6way has 172 edges; the strings 'method'/'word'/'cosine' appear NOWHERE in the file (edges carry only {a,b,comparison,score}; provenance carries only member_sha256). GET .../corpus-graph and .../phyletic-tree both resolve and are built from this word-derived graph.

4) Stored sweep is word_overlap: sweeps/8a555cc5f398.json has metric:'word_overlap'; screenshot 02-07-corpus-sweep.png shows Metric='word overlap (token)' and persisted run '8a555cc5f398 | word_overlap · high-recall (15/15)'.

5) Provenance gap real: edge dicts (corpus_graph.py:293) and graph provenance omit method; the per-comparison matrix is written under the generic name 'cross_similarity' (server.py:2749) by the word branch, so even the stored matrix name doesn't distinguish word from cosine. corpus-graph POST endpoint (server.py:2398) accepts only anchor_trim — no method/metric param.

Severity calibration: the collection IS cosine-available — GET .../congruence?metric=cosine returns all_congruent:true (all 6 members MLX-embedded/comparable), and the UI badge reads 'congruent · cosine'. So the designed cosine signal exists and is comparable, yet the entire analytic output (comparisons→graph→core/shell/singleton→phyletic tree→persisted sweep) is exclusively word-overlap-derived and cosine was never run through the pipeline. This is a validation-integrity defect on the flagship validation collection, and provenance cannot even distinguish which signal produced the results. Note the finding's framing 'direct consequence of finding #1 (semantic alignment broken)' is a cross-finding dependency; the demonstrated fact here (word-only downstream + cosine never exercised + missing method provenance) holds independently of whether #1 is a break vs merely not-run. One small over-statement: the sweep already exposes a Metric selector (SweepRequest.metric, server.py:176), so 'expose method as a sweep parameter' is partly satisfied for the sweep — but not for the corpus-graph endpoint. This does not materially reduce the finding. High severity is warranted.

findings.title: run_alignment lacks the congruence fail-loud gate that the probe endpoint enforces (silent cross-space matrix possible)
findings.evidence: POST /api/collections/{id}/probe explicitly catches MetricCongruenceError -> 409 (server.py:2472-2479, docstring 'fail-loud (409) ... never a silent cross-key probe'). POST /api/alignment/run (server.py:2712-2762) does NO congruence check; compute_cross_similarity only validates dim_a==dim_b (cross_similarity.py:32), so two texts embedded with DIFFERENT models but equal dim (2560) would silently yield a garbage cosine matrix instead of a 409.
findings.recommendation: Gate run_alignment's semantic/jaccard branch on operands_congruent(metric, cap_a, cap_b) (collections_ops.py:198) and raise 409 on mismatch, mirroring the probe contract.
findings.verify_reasoning: Verified against the real code paths (paths corrected from server.py:XXXX to core/palimpsest/*). CONFIRMED core claim: POST /api/collections/{id}/probe catches MetricCongruenceError -> 409 (server.py:2516-2517), and its docstring promises 'fail-loud (409)... never a silent cross-key probe' (2477); sweep has the identical gate (2541-2542); a congruence-report endpoint exists (2378). By contrast POST /api/alignment/run (server.py:2712-2790) has NO congruence check anywhere in its chain — grep for MetricCongruence/operands_congruent/congruence_key across alignment/ returns zero matches. Its default method 'semantic' (AlignmentRequest.method default, server.py:137) runs the else-branch calling compute_cross_similarity(proj_a, proj_b, 'cosine') (2756), and compute_cross_similarity validates ONLY dim_a!=dim_b (cross_similarity.py:32) with no model/fingerprint comparison. So two projects embedded by different models but equal dim (e.g. 2560) would yield a silent garbage cosine matrix instead of a 409 — exactly as reported. The congruence primitive the recommendation names (operands_congruent, collections_ops.py:198; congruence_key folds in model_fingerprint at 189-195) genuinely exists and is the correct tool.\n\nADJUSTMENTS (why high is slightly overstated, hence severity lowered to medium): (1) The recommendation is directionally right but NOT a drop-in one-liner. The alignment path loads a HARDCODED cache/embeddings.db (cross_similarity.py:75), not the label/layer-resolved store (embeddings_{label}.db) that member_embedding_capability reads; alignment never resolves a per-project capability object, so wiring operands_congruent requires plumbing capability resolution into the alignment flow, not just adding a guard. (2) The finding UNDER-reports scope: a second embedding-capable caller, masked_cross_similarity (collections_masking.py:238), is equally ungated. (3) Exploitability requires a deliberate mixed-embedding-model setup with coincidentally-equal dims; it is a silent-correctness defect (plausible-but-meaningless matrix), not a crash or security issue. (4) On the cited focus collection matthew-mark-6way, GET /api/collections confirms all 6 members resolve and per the substrate all are Qwen3-Embedding-4B dim2560 (congruent), so no garbage manifests there today — the defect is a missing guardrail, not active corruption. Net: a real, asymmetric contract gap worth fixing, best rated medium.

findings.title: compute_cross_similarity silently falls back to cosine for unknown metrics, violating the codebase's fail-loud principle
findings.evidence: cross_similarity.py:44-46: else branch logs 'Unknown similarity metric %s, falling back to cosine' and computes cosine. This contradicts sibling endpoints that reject unknowns loudly (projection 400 for non-pca, server.py:1624; distances 400 for bad kind, 1641) and the project's documented 'reject loudly rather than silently substitute' stance.
findings.recommendation: Raise ValueError for any metric not in {cosine,jaccard}; let the caller surface it as 400/409. A silent substitution mislabels the resulting matrix's provenance.

findings.title: corpus-graph/phyletic-tree/projection/corpus-analyses return 'not built' 404 for a non-existent collection (missing 404 vs not-built 404 conflated)
findings.evidence: Live: GET /api/collections/NOPE/phyletic-tree -> 404 {"detail":"Corpus graph not built; POST to build it first"} (server.py:2450); same for corpus-graph GET (2425), projection (2436), corpus-analyses (2467). read_corpus_graph returns None both for a missing collection and an unbuilt graph, so the caller cannot distinguish 'collection does not exist' from 'graph not built'. congruence correctly distinguishes (NOPE -> 404 'Collection not found', server.py:2391).

findings.title: /api/comparisons is workspace-global with no collection scoping; ids are directory names only

findings.title: matrix.bin ships no shape/dtype headers — binary contract depends on a separate JSON fetch
