dimensions.title: Comp-ling: alignment, embedding & similarity correctness
dimensions.summary: The low-level kernels are individually sound (cosine is correctly L2-normalized and clipped in cross_similarity.py:93-105; Waterman-Eggert non-overlap traceback and the max_alignments-with-WARNING behavior are correctly implemented in smith_waterman.py; the KJV verse-paragraph fix holds — GEN-MT↔KJV-MT now yields one full diagonal q=[15,1071) t=[15,1071), score 519, and GEN-MK↔KJV-MK yields q=[0,678), score 280). But the END-TO-END pipeline on this collection produces linguistically WRONG downstream results. Three compounding defects: (1) every one of the 275 stored records ships p_value=1.0 because the server only Gumbel-tests the semantic branch, not the word branch that actually generated this collection; (2) SW is invoked with score_threshold=0.0, so cross-book synoptic NOISE alignments (Mt↔Mk, scores 0.17–2.6) become homology edges that union Matthew anchors to Mark anchors — the "1 core" pangenome result is achieved for the wrong reason; (3) the phyletic distance is pure component co-membership Jaccard and discards alignment score/identity entirely, so the near-identical GEN-MT↔KJV-MT pair (score 519) lands at distance 0.750 — nearly the FARTHEST pair — and the tree cannot root DR as the outgroup. The ground-truth signal the collection was built to exercise is inverted.
strengths: Cosine kernel is numerically correct: per-row L2 normalization with a 1e-8 zero-guard, matmul, and explicit np.clip to [-1,1] (cross_similarity.py:93-105); same pattern in self_similarity._cosine_matrix (:114-120). Dimension mismatch fails loud (:32-36).

The KJV chapter-vs-verse paragraph regression is genuinely fixed: live probe confirms GEN-MT↔KJV-MT now returns ONE full-length diagonal record q=[15,1071) t=[15,1071) score=519.17 and GEN-MK↔KJV-MK returns q=[0,678) score=279.76, exactly the single-clean-diagonal behavior expected for same-versification near-identical pairs (/api/alignment records).

Smith-Waterman correctly implements Waterman-Eggert cell-consuming non-overlap traceback with a two-axis overlap-fraction duplicate rejector (smith_waterman.py:99-161), and the previously-flagged silent min(100,n*m) cap is replaced with max_alignments=None default plus a WARNING on truncation (:123-192) — the audit's cap concern is resolved.

build_corpus_graph correctly scopes to collection.project_ids member pairs only (corpus_graph.py:228-230), so the stale parent-project comparison cmp-e5415fdb (103 records, the two combined-book PARENT projects) does NOT contaminate the 6-way graph.

Provenance and reproducibility are strong: LOCKED_CONSTANTS (LASTZ seed/samples/percentile/floor) are declared and written into the signal manifest (self_similarity.py:57-75,1132-1149), and the stage-then-commit .partial/os.replace pattern (:963-1168) prevents orphaned .bin files on mid-run failure.

findings.title: Every alignment record on this collection ships p_value=1.0 — the word method has NO significance test
findings.evidence: server.py:2744-2766 (Gumbel calibrate_gumbel/p_value applied only in the else/semantic branch, never the elif method=='word' branch); live probe: all 275 records across every comparison have pValue==1.0, methods={'word':275} (/api/comparisons + /api/alignment/*/records)
findings.recommendation: Hoist the calibrate_gumbel(matrix) + per-record p_value assignment out of the semantic-only branch so it also runs for word (and alphabet). Until then, the max_p_value filter (server.py:2834), records_to_paf MAPQ (records.py:104-107), and any 'significant alignment' claim are inert for the entire validation collection — a p=1.0 score-519 near-identity is indistinguishable from a p=1.0 score-0.2 noise hit.
findings.verify_reasoning:
CONFIRMED by code + live API. Code (core/palimpsest/server.py:2742-2766): calibrate_gumbel + per-record p_value are assigned ONLY in the else/semantic branch (2764-2766). The elif method=='word' branch (2744-2753) computes matrix and runs sw_align but never touches p_value; the alphabet branch (2742-2743) likewise. Records therefore keep the dataclass default p_value=1.0 (core/palimpsest/alignment/records.py:45). Live probe of :8092 across all 16 comparisons: TOTAL 275 records, methods={'word':275}, pValue distribution={1.0:275}, scores range 0.104–519.169 — a p=1.0 score-519 near-identity is indistinguishable from a p=1.0 score-0.1 noise hit, exactly as claimed. Downstream inertness confirmed live: GET /api/alignment/{q}/{t}/records?max_p_value=0.05 returns 0 of 3 records (filter server.py:2834-2835 rejects everything at any real cutoff); records.py:104-107,132 derive PAF MAPQ = -10*log10(1.0) = 0 for every exported row; CircosView.tsx:216 renders 'p=1.00e+0' in every arc tooltip, presenting fabricated non-significance to the user. The fix is trivially feasible: calibrate_gumbel (gumbel.py:17) is matrix-agnostic and the word branch already holds `matrix`, so hoisting the two lines above the branch works for word.

Two scope refinements (finding slightly overstated): (1) The '(and alphabet)' half of the recommendation is not a simple hoist — the alphabet branch (line 2743) produces no similarity matrix, so calibrate_gumbel cannot be applied identically there. (2) The claim that 'any significant alignment claim is inert for the entire collection' overreaches on the collection's headline deliverable: the pangenome corpus-graph and phyletic tree consume r.score, NOT r.p_value (corpus_graph.py:257), so the core/shell/singleton pangenome and NJ tree are unaffected by this bug. Impact is real but scoped to the max_p_value filter, PAF MAPQ export, and the Circos p-value tooltip. Score-based thresholding remains fully functional (scores endpoint returns valid suggested_threshold=0.35, max=0.50).

Severity: kept at high. A statistical significance test that silently defaults to p=1.0 for the exact method (word) used on the flagship validation collection is precisely the kind of broken-but-plausible output a scientific reviewer would trust; it makes the significance affordance a lie across all 275 records. Not critical because the primary pangenome/tree result and score-based filtering are intact — no data corruption of the core deliverable.

findings.title: SW score_threshold=0.0 admits cross-book synoptic NOISE as homology edges, collapsing Mt+Mk into one bogus core
findings.evidence: server.py:2752 calls sw_align with no score_threshold (default 0.0, smith_waterman.py:26). corpus-graph shows 172 edges incl. cross-book Mt↔Mk edges at scores 0.17–2.61 (e.g. GEN-MK↔GEN-MT 18 edges 0.22–1.72, KJV-MK↔KJV-MT 14 edges 0.17–1.65). Component c7 is the single 'core' reaching all 6 members purely because these noise edges bridge Matthew↔Mark anchors (.scratch/audit6/_graph.json summary core=1)
findings.recommendation: The '1 core / 1 shell / 6 singleton' headline is reached for the WRONG reason. Set a positive score_threshold (or, once fixed, a p-value cutoff) before records become homology anchors in corpus_graph. Different books that share only synoptic paraphrase should NOT co-occur in a core component; they do here only because a score≈0.2 cross-book hit counts identically to a score≈519 same-book hit.
findings.verify_reasoning:
Every load-bearing claim checks out against code, captured evidence, and the LIVE server.

CODE: smith_waterman.py:26 has score_threshold: float = 0.0 (exactly as cited). server.py:2729 imports smith_waterman as sw_align; both call sites (word path 2752, semantic path 2761) pass NO score_threshold, so default 0.0 is used. (Minor citation slip: 2752 is the word path; the semantic path is 2761 — but the substance is correct.) corpus_graph.py build_corpus_graph reads ALL alignment.jsonl records and unions any two anchors sharing an edge (lines 247-293) with ZERO score or p-value gate — grep of corpus_graph.py shows no p_value reference at all. Notably, p-values ARE computed per record (server.py:2766) and the pairwise alignment-view endpoint CAN filter by min_score/max_p_value (2826-2835), but that statistical apparatus is entirely bypassed when records become homology anchors — exactly the auditor's point.

NUMBERS: I re-derived from .scratch/audit6/_graph.json AND confirmed against the LIVE server (http://localhost:8092/api/collections/matthew-mark-6way/corpus-graph): 172 edges, 1 core / 1 shell / 6 singleton, edge scores 0.10–519.17. Classifying edges by book: 66 cross-book Mt<->Mk edges scoring 0.158–1.716 (GEN-MK<->GEN-MT 18 edges, KJV-MK<->KJV-MT 14 edges — matches the cited 0.17–1.72 / 18 / 14 figures) vs 106 same-book edges reaching 519.

DECISIVE TEST (causation, not just correlation): I rebuilt the union-find keeping ONLY same-book edges. Result: the graph splits into a clean Matthew cluster {DR-MT,GEN-MT,KJV-MT} and a separate Mark cluster {DR-MK,GEN-MK,KJV-MK} — NO core. The single core c7 reaching all 6 members exists ONLY because the weak cross-book edges bridge Matthew<->Mark. Threshold sweep confirms: at any threshold < 1.716 the core stays at 1 (bridged); at threshold >= 1.72 the bridge breaks and the largest component reaches only 3 members (the correct outgroup structure). So the '1 core / 1 shell / 6 singleton' headline is genuinely reached for the WRONG reason: a score~0.2 cross-book synoptic-paraphrase hit counts identically to a score~519 same-book near-verbatim hit.

Tests (test_corpus_graph.py) confirm the design has no score gate and use synthetic score=30 fixtures that never surface the noise problem — the invariant test even asserts every edge-touched component is core/shell, entrenching that any edge = homology. Ground truth (Geneva/KJV near-identical sisters, DR Vulgate outgroup, Mt/Mk share content not wording) means Mt and Mk should NOT co-occur in a core; they do here only via noise.

Severity: the finding materially corrupts the flagship corpus-tier output (core/shell/singleton classification and, downstream, the phyletic tree which reads component membership). It is not a crash or data-loss issue and is confined to the reference-free corpus graph, so high (not critical) is the right level. Recommendation (positive score_threshold, or gate anchors by the already-computed p_value before they enter corpus_graph) is sound and directly implementable.

findings.title: Phyletic distance discards alignment score/identity — near-identical GEN-MT↔KJV-MT lands at distance 0.750 (nearly the farthest pair)
findings.evidence: phylo.component_distance_matrix (analysis/phylo.py:33-52) computes D[i,j]=1-|comps with both|/|comps with either| using ONLY component co-membership — score/identity never enter. Computed from live _graph.json: GEN-MT↔KJV-MT=0.750, GEN-MT↔DR-MT=0.667, KJV-MT↔GEN-MK=0.500. GEN-MT's nearest neighbor is DR-MT/GEN-MK (0.667), the true-sister KJV-MT ranks 4th (0.750). Screenshot 03-congruence.png shows the resulting tree does NOT root DR as outgroup and places GEN/KJV at scrambled leaves.
findings.recommendation: A near-identical pair (score 519, identity 0.75) and a noise pair (score 0.5) both contribute exactly one shared-component edge, so the tree is blind to edge weight. Weight the distance by aligned coverage or mean identity (e.g. 1 - normalized-alignment-score), not bare component-set Jaccard, or the neighbor-joining tree cannot recover the documented Geneva≈KJV / DR-outgroup topology.
findings.verify_reasoning:
Verified against code, live API, screenshot, and raw alignment data.

CODE: component_distance_matrix (core/palimpsest/analysis/phylo.py:33-52 — the finding's `analysis/phylo.py` resolves here) computes D[i,j]=1-both/union using ONLY comp_member_sets co-membership. graph.components is built by union-find over ALL alignment edges regardless of score (corpus_graph.py:288-293 unions any linked anchor pair; the only gate is optional anchor_trim, default 0.0). Edges DO store the score (corpus_graph.py:293) but phyletic_tree (corpus_graph.py:404-406) never reads it — comp_sets are pure membership. test_phylo.py:33 hardcodes D[0,2]==0.75 for share-one-core, confirming the metric is intentional Jaccard.

LIVE API (:8092 read-only, matthew-mark-6way, member order Matt1=DR,Matt2=Geneva,Matt3=KJV,Mark1=DR,Mark2=Geneva,Mark3=KJV): distances match the finding EXACTLY — GEN-MT↔KJV-MT=0.750, GEN-MT↔DR-MT=0.667, KJV-MT↔GEN-MK=0.500. GEN-MT's nearest neighbors are all 0.667 (DR-MT, GEN-MK, KJV-MK); the true sister KJV-MT ranks 4th at 0.750. Tree topology (rooted DR-MT): GEN-MT and KJV-MT are NOT sisters — KJV-MT sits deep beside the Mark clade (node0={GEN-MK,KJV-MK}); the documented Geneva≈KJV pairing within Matthew is not recovered.

ROOT CAUSE: the corpus graph collapses to just 8 components (6 singletons + 1 shell {DR-MT,GEN-MT} + 1 core spanning all 6 members). Union-find transitive-closure merges the near-identical Matthew alignment and cross-book synoptic noise into the same 6-member core, so nearly every pair shares exactly 1 component and the Jaccard signal degenerates into a function of singleton-residue participation counts, not homology depth.

SCREENSHOT 03-congruence.png: all-pairs matrix shows one '2' (DR-MT↔GEN-MT) and '1' everywhere else; the rendered phyletic tree shows Geneva-Matthew and KJV-Matthew as non-sisters — consistent with the API topology.

RECOMMENDATION SOUNDNESS: I read the raw alignment.jsonl scores in .scratch/validation-mm/.comparisons — they span 0.42 to 519.17. The near-identical pair scores 519.17 (matches the finding's cited 'score 519'); the noise pair max 0.5 (matches cited 0.5). Both contribute exactly one component edge, so the tree is blind to ~3 orders of magnitude of edge weight. Weighting distance by mean identity / normalized alignment score (as recommended) would clearly separate the 519 pair from the 0.5 pair.

NUANCES (do not undermine the finding): (1) This is not a coding error — the build journal (collections-tier-build-journal.md:203-207, Autonomous decision #1) documents the Jaccard-over-components choice as intentional, to keep the tree 'a reading of the graph's own structure.' But it demonstrably fails its documented FR-38 purpose on the flagship ground-truth collection, so it is a real methodological/correctness defect. (2) The finding's phrase 'does not root DR as outgroup' is slightly loose: DR-MT IS the suggested/default root (most component-complete). The tree is still scrambled and fails to recover Geneva≈KJV, so the substance holds.

findings.title: Score is proportional to alignment length — scores are incomparable across pairs of different length
findings.evidence: smith_waterman.py:73-81 accumulates score=sim*2-1 per aligned cell with no length normalization. Live: GEN-MT↔KJV-MT score=519 (1056 aligned paras) vs GEN-MK↔KJV-MK score=280 (678 paras) — the ~1.9x ratio is the paragraph-count ratio, not a similarity difference (both are near-identical, identity 0.75 vs 0.71). /api/alignment/.../scores returns suggested_threshold==the single score (519) for one-record pairs, a degenerate cutoff.
findings.recommendation: Raw SW score cannot be compared or thresholded across pairs of unequal length. Surface a length-normalized score (score/aligned_length) or bits-per-column alongside the raw score for any cross-pair ranking, corpus-graph edge weighting, or the FR-40 empirical dotplot cutoff.

findings.title: DR↔Geneva diagonal is shredded into 34 fragments by the sim*2-1 zero-point at identity 0.5
findings.evidence: smith_waterman.py:74 maps identity 0.5 -> score 0.0. DR-MT↔GEN-MT records (live, sorted by queryStart) show one block [15,473) then a cascade of 2–9-para fragments ALL at a constant +1 target offset after one drift at para ~665, each at identity 0.48–0.50 (target-offset distribution {0:5, 1:34}). This is a SINGLE continuous shifted diagonal chopped up because per-cell scores hover at ~0 and H keeps resetting, not 34 distinct homology events.
findings.recommendation: The 'DR fragments at drift points' story is only half-true: there is one real versification drift (+1) but the 34-way fragmentation is an artifact of the identity-0.5 zero-point plus gap handling, not 34 drifts. Lower the score midpoint (e.g. map identity via a lower baseline, or reduce gap_open) so a genuinely continuous cross-translation diagonal survives as one record; otherwise DR anchors are over-fragmented before merge and the fragment count misleads.

findings.title: Alignment sub-tab shows 'Ready to align' even when records exist on disk; dotplot uses cosine while records use word
findings.evidence: screenshot 07-compare-alignment.png: GEN-MT vs KJV-MT shows 'Ready to align / Select a method and click Align' with method dropdown defaulting to 'Semantic (SBERT)', yet /api/alignment/.../records returns the score-519 word record. screenshot 07-compare-dotplot.png renders the cosine cross-similarity matrix (heavy full-field haze + diagonal) — a different matrix/method than the stored word records the user would compare against.
findings.recommendation: The default method (Semantic) mismatches the method that actually populated this collection (word), so the user sees an empty alignment panel over a cosine dotplot while valid word records sit on disk. Auto-load existing records for the pair (any method) and label the dotplot with the method whose records are shown, so the viewer isn't silently comparing a cosine heatmap against word alignments.

findings.title: compute_word_overlap uses raw whitespace-split token sets — no stopword/punctuation filtering, unlike self_similarity
findings.evidence: cross_similarity._word_overlap_similarity (:113) uses set(t.lower().split()) — punctuation stays attached and stopwords are kept, whereas self_similarity._content_tokens (:99-103) strips punctuation and STOPWORDS. Consequence: cross-text word-overlap identity for DR↔Geneva paragraphs sits at ~0.49–0.50 (dominated by shared function words like 'and/the/of'), which is exactly the 0.5 zero-point that drives finding #5's fragmentation.
findings.recommendation: Align the two word-overlap implementations: filter punctuation and stopwords in cross_similarity as self_similarity already does. Content-word Jaccard would push genuine same-verse pairs well above 0.5 (surviving the sim*2-1 midpoint) and push unrelated pairs lower, sharpening both the diagonal and the noise floor that finding #2 depends on.

findings.title: Stale parent-project comparisons pollute /api/comparisons (orphaned two-book records)
findings.evidence: /api/comparisons lists cmp-e5415fdb6187b13e (query ...chapter-in-book-0047-book-0048 = DR combined-book PARENT, 39,958 words; target ...mark-book-matthew = Geneva PARENT), record_count 103, max score 35.67 — a comparison between combined Matthew+Mark parent projects, not 6-way members. These are correctly excluded from the graph (corpus_graph.py:228-230) but confuse any consumer that enumerates /api/comparisons.
findings.recommendation: These orphaned parent-project comparisons are harmless to the graph but misleading in the comparisons list and score aggregation (their 35.67 max mimics a real same-book score at the cross-book parent level). Tag comparisons with their owning collection/member scope, or prune comparisons not between current collection members, so the comparisons index reflects only the intended member matrix.

dimensions.title: Comp-ling: masking, verses, OffsetMap & lexical stats
dimensions.summary: The computational-linguistics substrate is mathematically sound and well-engineered. All lexical-diversity indices (TTR, MATTR, MTLD, Yule's K, Zipf slope, Heaps' law) verify exactly against their canonical literature definitions; MTLD reproduces McCarthy & Jarvis (2010) to machine precision. The OffsetMap coordinate system is provably lossless (30,844 randomized round-trips, 0 failures) with correct gap-bridging inverse_span semantics, and KWIC original-coordinate remapping is exact even on members with masked verse numbers and pilcrows. The KJV verse-number rebuild is correct: no digit tokens leak into analyzable text, multi-digit spans ("10","25") are masked precisely, and the "heaven.4" abutting-marker regex handles red-letter cases. Two genuine correctness bugs exist: (1) exact-repeat phrase keys are corrupted by empty normalized tokens (double/leading spaces), confirmed leaking to the live /duplicates endpoint on the Geneva member; (2) the Dunning G2 helper zeroes a whole log-likelihood term when a contingency cell count is 0, understating association strength for perfect collocations.
strengths: Lexical-diversity formulas are literature-correct: MTLD exactly reproduces the bidirectional McCarthy & Jarvis (2010) algorithm (verified against a reference impl over randomized inputs, |diff|<1e-6, incl. the all-unique factors=0 -> N convention); Yule's K matches K=10^4*(sum i^2*V(i)-N)/N^2; MATTR matches Covington & McFall sliding-window mean; Zipf slope ~= -1.013 for a synthetic zipfian sample; Heaps returns 0<beta<1 (textstats.py:66-129).

OffsetMap is a rigorously correct coordinate layer: 30,844 translate/inverse_point round-trips passed with 0 failures; inverse_span gap-bridging returns (first_char_orig, last_char_orig+1) as designed; construction enforces the ordered/disjoint/non-empty precondition with ValueError (derive.py:48-142).

Verse-number masking is content-preserving and reversible for the rebuilt KJV layer: p.analyzable_text() yields 0 standalone digit tokens across 1071 verses (1890 masked chars), all num tokens are pure digits, and the bare-number regex (?<![0-9A-Za-z])(\d{1,3})(?![0-9]) correctly handles the abutting 'heaven.4 Blessed' and 'clothed?32(' red-letter cases (.scratch/build_kjv_mm.py:182).

KWIC/dispersion coordinate remap is exact: every returned original [start,end) span in /kwic (verified on the Geneva member which carries masked verse numbers + 103 pilcrows) matches the keyword byte-for-byte against reference.txt (0/8 mismatches).

The verse-paragraph fix holds across the collection: KJV Matthew integrity reports 1071 paragraphs == 1071 verses, DR Matthew masking header shows 1070 paragraphs (Vulgate versification), and the corpus pangenome badge reads the expected '1 core / 1 shell / 6 singleton' (02-05-corpus-masking.png).

findings.title: Exact-repeat phrase keys corrupted by empty normalized tokens (double/leading/trailing spaces)
findings.evidence: tracks/repeats.py:88 (key = " ".join(gram)); confirmed live: GET /api/projects/<geneva-matt>/duplicates?min_words=3&min_occurrences=3 returns 12 phrase keys with a leading space, e.g. "' again the kingdom of heaven is'"
findings.recommendation: _normalise() (repeats.py:64-67) maps punctuation-only tokens (the Geneva member has 103 whitespace-isolated '¶' pilcrows that survive the \S+ tokenizer) to empty strings. In _count_repeats these empties become interior/boundary blanks so `" ".join(gram)` yields double-space or leading/trailing-space keys, and the later `phrase.split()` (repeats.py:160, 207) silently drops them (an n-gram key round-trips to fewer tokens, corrupting plen). Fix: skip grams containing any empty token (`if any(w == "" for w in gram): continue`) OR filter empties before joining and re-derive plen from the joined-then-split key consistently. This inflates /duplicates phrase_count and shows malformed keys to users; masking survives only by accident via fragmentary sub-keys.

findings.title: Dunning G2 log-likelihood zeroes an entire term when a cell count is 0, understating association
findings.evidence: analysis/textstats.py:188-191 (_ll: `if k <= 0 or p <= 0 or p >= 1: return 0.0`); reproduced: _log_likelihood(3,3,3,10)=7.2238 vs canonical 2x2 Dunning=12.2173
findings.recommendation: The `k <= 0` guard drops the whole term when k=0, but the correct value is 0*ln(p) + (total-k)*ln(1-p) = total*ln(1-p), which is nonzero (e.g. _ll(0,7,0.3) should be 7*ln(0.7)=-2.4967, not 0). The k*ln(p) sub-term legitimately vanishes as x*ln(x)->0, but the (total-k)*ln(1-p) sub-term must be kept. This systematically understates Dunning's G2 for bigrams with a zero contingency cell (all c12==c1 perfect-collocation cases tested differ by ~5 points). It is display-only (collocations rank by count, textstats.py:224), so it mis-labels the reported G2 without reordering. Fix: return `(k*log(p) if k>0 else 0.0) + ((total-k)*log(1-p) if total-k>0 else 0.0)` guarding each sub-term independently.

findings.title: PMI uses token-count n rather than pair-count as the normalization base
findings.evidence: analysis/textstats.py:222 (pmi = math.log2((c * n) / (unigram[a] * unigram[b]))); verified: code PMI 1.737 vs standard windowed PMI 1.889 for a controlled corpus, delta = log2(n/N_pairs)
findings.recommendation: Standard windowed PMI is log2(P(a,b)/(P(a)P(b))) with P(a,b)=count/N_pairs and P(a)=uni[a]/n. The code substitutes N_pairs with n, adding a constant offset log2(n/N_pairs) to every pair's PMI (~0.15 for the toy corpus, smaller for real texts, larger for window>1 where N_pairs ~ n*window). Because the offset is constant for a fixed window, PMI *rankings are preserved*, so this is minor and consistent with the module's descriptive framing — but the absolute PMI values are biased high. Consider documenting the convention or dividing pair counts by the true windowed-pair total for literature comparability.

findings.title: OffsetMap.translate_point maps an exclusive-span-end offset ambiguously when sep_len==0
findings.evidence: derive.py:73-79 (translate_point uses `if off <= e`); reproduced with spans [(10,15),(20,25)], sep=0: translate_point(15)=5 but inverse_point(5)=20 (round-trip 15->5->20 asymmetric)
findings.recommendation: For a kept span [s,e), the offset off==e is the first char of the excised gap and has no content pre-image, yet translate_point returns base[i]+(e-s), which — when sep_len==0 (the analyzable_text default, project.py:346) — collides with the next span's content start. Current callers are safe: remap_verses passes verse text_end that equals a *content* end (round-trips correctly), analyzable_verse_spans uses remap_element (correct exclusive handling), and the integrity round-trip test only samples offsets strictly inside [s,e) (integrity.py:78). But this is a latent trap: any future caller passing an exclusive-end into translate_point on a sep=0 map gets a silent mistranslation. Recommend `if off < e` (return None at the exclusive end) and have exclusive-end callers use remap_element/inverse_span.

findings.title: verses.py detect_verses cannot regenerate the KJV/Geneva bare-number verse tracks (documented single-source drift)
findings.evidence: verses.py module docstring claims it is 'the single source' for the verse index and mask layer; detect_verses() returns 0 records on the KJV parent text (only matches ^C:V., verses.py:37), yet tracks/verses.jsonl has 1749 correct records written by .scratch/build_kjv_mm.py:167-207
findings.recommendation: The production verse-track writer server._write_verses_track (server.py:576-593) uses verses.py's C:V.-only detect_verses, which finds nothing in the bare-number '<num> <text>' KJV/Geneva format. Those tracks were built by a one-off .scratch script (build_kjv_mm.py) with a different regex and the correct multi-digit/abutting handling. Consequently, re-running the production verse pipeline on the KJV/Geneva parents would wipe all 1749 verses (0 detected), silently zeroing the just-fixed verse layer. The bare-number path lives in layout.py (detect_verse_regions/detect_versed_chapter_markers) but is not wired into _write_verses_track. Recommend either promoting the bare-number verse detector into verses.py/detect_verses (so the documented single source actually covers this dominant scripture format) or documenting that bare-number editions require the layout path, not _write_verses_track.

dimensions.title: Collections tier correctness (graph/phylo/probe/sweep)
dimensions.summary: The collections tier is a genuinely mature, well-documented reference-free/pangenome analysis stack: the congruence contract (collections_ops.py), probe gating (collections_probe.py), the NJ tree math (analysis/phylo.py), and the token/LSH sweep path are correctly implemented and honestly unit-tested. However, on the actual 6-way ground-truth collection the corpus graph over-merges catastrophically: all six members (both Matthew and Mark, three translations each) collapse into a single "core" homology component driven by ~66 weak cross-book synoptic edges, producing scientifically wrong pangenome (1 core spanning two distinct books), a degenerate distance matrix, and a phyletic tree that roots the DR outgroup as the ancestor. Separately, the embedding-family sweep reports estimated_recall=1.0 tautologically because candidate-gen and its oracle both rank by the same cosine — verified live on the 6-way (56,169-pair Matt2×Matt3 sweep → recall 1.0). The KJV verse-paragraph fix DID hold (all 6 members verse-paragraphed, alignments present, 172 edges), but the downstream graph/tree do not correctly reflect the intended biology.
strengths: Metric-congruence contract is rigorous and fail-loud: collections_probe.py:63-113 _gate_congruent_cohort refuses partial/mixed-space probes and even catches the fingerprints-agree-but-dims-disagree corruption case (probe.py:107-112); operands_congruent (collections_ops.py:198-214) returns actionable reconcile hints.

The neighbor-joining implementation (analysis/phylo.py:55-104) is a faithful, deterministic Saitou-Nei with correct Q-matrix, lowest-index tie-breaking, and principled negative-branch clamping (documented as a display artifact, phylo.py:59-60); the tree math is correct — the garbage comes from upstream degenerate distances, not the NJ.

The token/LSH sweep family is genuinely honest: the live word_overlap run on the 6-way (run 8a555cc5f398) reports mean_estimated_recall=0.0785 with real per-pair variance (0.012–0.236), because lsh_candidate_pairs approximates Jaccard differently than the exact-Jaccard oracle — a real measurement, not a tautology.

Recall reporting is structurally honest at the summary layer: summarize_candidates (candidate_gen.py:192-226) returns None (not a fabricated 1.0) when there is no oracle sample, and n_pruned is always reported so a cap is never silent; unit-tested with a genuine 0.5 partial-recall case (test_candidate_gen.py:106-110).

Non-destructive run versioning + identity-based staleness (collections_ops.py:346-421) is content-addressed with no wall-clock, so a ground-truth-masking re-run correctly surfaces as a new identity + stale prior rather than a silent overwrite.

findings.title: Corpus graph falsely merges Matthew and Mark into ONE core component via unthresholded weak cross-book edges
findings.evidence: GET :8092/api/collections/matthew-mark-6way/corpus-graph → components: c7 classification=core members=[all 6], node_ids span n1(Matt1 para[15,1056)), n5(Matt2), n6(Matt3) AND n7(Mark1 para[0,676)), n8(Mark2), n9(Mark3). Edge analysis: 66 cross-book Mt↔Mk edges (mean score 0.609) vs same-book (mean 22.3); corpus_graph.py:288-293 unions every alignment record with NO score threshold, so a handful of weak synoptic matches transitively fuse two distinct books. Ground truth expected a per-book core, not a Matt+Mark fusion.
findings.recommendation: Add a score/similarity threshold on which edges are eligible to union in build_corpus_graph (corpus_graph.py:288-293) — e.g. drop edges below a percentile of same-comparison scores, or a minimum trimmed-block similarity — so weak cross-book synteny records still appear as edges/shell links but do not collapse whole books into one core.
findings.verify_reasoning: Verified all three grounding paths. CODE: corpus_graph.py:288-293 (build_corpus_graph, the raw_edges union loop) unions na/nb for every stored alignment record with zero score/similarity gate — confirmed by reading the file; the only edge-honesty knob (anchor_trim, C6a) operates on SW boundary-cell cross-similarity, not on record score. API: GET :8092/api/collections/matthew-mark-6way/corpus-graph returns component c7 classification="core" spanning all 6 members with node_ids n1(DR-Matt para[15,1056)), n5(Gen-Matt), n6(KJV-Matt) AND n7(DR-Mark para[0,676)), n8(Gen-Mark), n9(KJV-Mark) — exactly as the finding states. EDGE STATS reproduced: 66 cross-book edges mean 0.609 (max 1.716) vs same-book mean ~22.3 (I measured 22.34); the two populations are cleanly separable (all 66 cross-book edges < 2.0). FIX VALIDATION: I re-simulated union-find with a score gate on the live edges — threshold >=2.0 eliminates the false 6-member core and resolves into the ground-truth per-book clusters {DR,Gen,KJV}-Matt and {DR,Gen,KJV}-Mark with structure intact, confirming the recommended fix works. The finding is NOT redundant with existing machinery: I ran build_corpus_graph with anchor_trim=0.0/0.5/0.8/0.95 — the false core PERSISTS at 0.5 and 0.8 and only collapses at 0.95 while simultaneously destroying nearly all real structure (n_edges 172->2), so anchor_trim does not cover this failure mode; a score/percentile threshold is materially better. Behavior is as-designed (all 14 corpus_graph tests pass), so this is a design gap, not a regression. Scoping caveats that keep it from being an unqualified critical: (1) the graph is not one giant component — the defect is specifically the false core; shells/singletons exist. (2) A naive global score cutoff also drops ~half of legitimate same-book edges (53/106 are <2.0), so the finding's own more-principled per-comparison-percentile suggestion is the correct framing rather than a flat cutoff. (3) There is a defensible architectural view that the correspondence-quality gate belongs upstream at C2 alignment (which already exposes score_threshold, defaulting to 0.0) and that display already applies a 75th-pct min_score, making C3 the place the noise leaks through unfiltered. (4) DR-outgroup labeling/embedding noise (DR-Mark<->Gen-Matt scored higher than DR-Mark<->Gen-Mark) hints at an upstream alignment-quality issue, but does not affect the C3 union defect. This is a domain/analysis-correctness bug (the C3 tier's headline pangenome classification is scientifically wrong under defaults), not a crash/security/data-loss issue, and correct output is reachable via existing knobs — so high, not critical.

findings.title: Monolithic anchor merging destroys passage-level homology granularity (only 16 nodes / 8 components from 172 edges)
findings.evidence: corpus_graph.py:267 _merge_intervals collapses ALL of a member's aligned intervals into maximal ranges: node dump shows n1 = Matt1(DR) para[15,1056) is a SINGLE node covering ~1041 paragraphs; n5,n7,n8,n9 are similarly whole-book anchors. corpus-graph summary: n_nodes=16, n_components=8 for a collection with hundreds of verse-level alignments. Because each member is essentially one giant anchor, any single cross-member edge fuses entire members (root cause of the false core). anchor_trim (default 0.0, server.py:2400) only trims block boundaries and cannot fix this.
findings.recommendation: Anchor at alignment-block granularity rather than merging all intervals per member: keep distinct aligned blocks as separate PassageNodes (or split merged intervals at edge boundaries) so the graph produces the intended per-passage homology components instead of one-node-per-member.
findings.verify_reasoning:
FACTS CONFIRMED against code + live read-only API (:8092): corpus_graph.py:267 _merge_intervals collapses each member's intervals into maximal ranges (verified by reading it, lines 123-134). Live GET /api/collections/matthew-mark-6way/corpus-graph returns n_nodes=16, n_edges=172, n_components=8, core=1, shell=1, singleton=6; 6 of 16 nodes are whole-book anchors (span>400 paras: n1 DR-Matt=1041, n5/n6 Gen/KJV-Matt=1056, n7/n8/n9 Mark whole-book). Union-find trace confirms the Matthew cluster (n1,n2,n3,n5,n6) and Mark cluster (n7,n8,n9) are fused into ONE 'core' component via 66 weak Matt-Mark synoptic bridge edges (scores 0.16-1.72). anchor_trim default 0.0 (server.py:2400) only trims block boundaries (_trim_to_high_sim, lines 150-168) and cannot break whole-book anchors — confirmed. So every factual particular in the EVIDENCE is accurate.

WHY PARTIAL / OVERSTATED: (1) The CLAIM frames _merge_intervals as a bug, but it is documented, tested, INTENDED design. Module docstring (lines 4-5) defines a node as a 'maximal aligned paragraph range within a member,' and test_corpus_graph.py:20-22 explicitly states _merge_intervals fuses adjacent ranges and that unaligned gaps are the load-bearing separator. Whole-book collapse here is a consequence of dense verse-level coverage with tiny (1-3 para) inter-verse gaps, not a coding defect. (2) 'Destroys granularity'/'false core' is overstated: I ran the live phyletic-tree endpoint — it still recovers real ground truth. Geneva-Mark and KJV-Mark come out at Jaccard distance 0.000 (correct near-identical sisters), participation counts differ meaningfully per member (DR-Mt=5 ... KJV-Mk=1), and the full 6x6 distance matrix distinguishes every member. It is one-node-per-member for 3 members but 4 anchors for DR-Matt; coarse, not destroyed. (3) The proposed fix (block-granularity nodes / split at edge boundaries) would NOT by itself fix the Matt/Mark fusion, because union-find fuses whole components on ANY single edge regardless of node size; the genuine (if weak) synoptic Matt-Mark content edges would still bridge unless a score threshold is also added — the recommendation is therefore incomplete.

REAL RESIDUAL ISSUE: coarse whole-book anchoring on dense-coverage corpora does limit expression of per-pericope homology, and fusing Matthew+Mark into a single all-member 'core' is a legitimate limitation for this synoptic use case. Worth surfacing as a design limitation, but it is known/documented behavior mitigated by the downstream distance analysis — not a critical correctness defect in _merge_intervals.

findings.title: Embedding-family sweep estimated_recall is tautologically 1.0 (candidate-gen and oracle both rank by cosine, depth >= top_n)
findings.evidence: candidate_gen.py: ann_candidate_pairs (line 83) returns top-depth by cosine; exact_top_pairs_cosine (line 156) returns top-top_n by cosine — SAME metric. collections_sweep.py:34 _RECALL_TOP_N=3; candidate_gen.py:34 _MODE_DEPTH={high-recall:20, fast:5}. Since depth(5,20) >= top_n(3), oracle ⊆ candidates per row → recall==1.0 by construction. Verified LIVE on the 6-way: Matt2×Matt3 real embedding sweep (56,169 pairs, non-dense, depth=20) → estimated_recall=1.0. Docstring (candidate_gen.py:9-11) claims 'empirical...never a theoretical hand-wave' — false for the embedding family.
findings.recommendation: Make the embedding oracle independent of the candidate generator's ranking (e.g. oracle = exact top-N over the FULL matrix while candidates use a genuine ANN index/approximation with recall loss), or explicitly flag embedding-family recall as 'exact by construction (depth>=oracle_topN)' rather than reporting it as a measured empirical number. As-is a user selecting cosine in the sweep UI on this all-embedded collection sees a reassuring ~100% recall that measures nothing.
findings.verify_reasoning: Independently verified all material claims. CODE: candidate_gen.py ann_candidate_pairs (L83-99) computes each A-row's top-`depth` B-neighbors by cosine (ua @ ub.T, L93-97); exact_top_pairs_cosine (L156-171) computes each sampled A-row's top-`top_n` B-neighbors by the SAME cosine over the SAME normalized ub — the recall oracle is the candidate generator's own ranking truncated shorter. summarize_candidates (L211-213) then reports |oracle∩candidates|/|oracle|. PARAMS: collections_sweep.py _RECALL_TOP_N=3 (L35); candidate_gen.py _MODE_DEPTH={high-recall:20, fast:5} (L34). Since depth (5 or 20) >= top_n (3) always, for every sampled row oracle top-3 ⊆ candidate top-depth (robust even under ties: a true top-3 element cannot be excluded from a top-d set for d>=5), so recall==1.0 by construction. REPRODUCED via core/.venv python: random 200x300 embeddings, depth=5 → recall=1.0 (59000 pruned), depth=20 → recall=1.0 (56000 pruned); recall only falls below 1.0 (0.667) when depth=2 < top_n=3, a value the code never uses. LIVE EMPIRICAL: workspace journal .scratch/validation-mm/collections/matthew-mark-validation/sweeps/368bd5c8d95e.json is a real metric=cosine, mode=high-recall, dense=False sweep (Geneva vs Douay-Rheims, n_pairs_total=149753, n_candidates=7820, prune_fraction=0.9478, depth=20) reporting estimated_recall=1.0 on a 147-row sample — a genuinely-pruning embedding sweep whose recall metric measures nothing. By contrast the word_overlap/MinHash sweeps in the same collection (journal 8a555cc5f398, and 5be231121c07) report meaningful recall values (0.0157, 0.051, 0.102, 0.2314) because that family uses genuinely different algorithms for candidates (LSH) vs oracle (exact Jaccard) — so the finding is correctly scoped to the embedding family only. DOCSTRING: candidate_gen.py L9-11 claims 'empirical estimated recall measured on a sample — never a silent cap, never a theoretical hand-wave'; the code only labels 'recall 1.0 by construction' for the DENSE case (L72, L203-207), never acknowledging the non-dense embedding case is equally tautological — so the honesty guarantee is contradicted for embeddings, as the finding states. TESTS: test_candidate_gen.py exercises summarize_candidates with hand-crafted candidate/oracle sets that deliberately differ (partial-recall test L106-110), but no test runs ann_candidate_pairs + exact_top_pairs_cosine together, so the tautology is not caught. The recall is surfaced to the UI/API via mean_estimated_recall (collections_sweep.py L245) and per-pair estimated_recall (L249). Minor discrepancy: the finding's illustrative '56,169 pairs / Matt2×Matt3' figure differs from the journal I found (149753 / Geneva×DR), but both are non-dense cosine sweeps in the same collection family showing recall=1.0 — a non-material example difference that does not affect correctness. Severity: this is a correctness/integrity defect in a user-facing reassurance metric (shows ~100% recall while pruning 95% of pairs), contradicting the module's own honesty contract, but it is not a crash/data-loss/security issue and the token family's recall is genuinely measured — high, not critical.

findings.title: suggested_root picks the DR outgroup as tree root because singleton fragmentation inflates participation
findings.evidence: corpus_graph.py:407-408 uses phylo.participation_counts as root heuristic; phylo.py:24-30 counts ALL components including singletons. Live phyletic-tree: participation={Matt1(DR):5, Matt2(Gen):3, Matt3(KJV):2, ...}; suggested_root=Matt1(DR). DR fragments most (Vulgate versification → 3 singleton gap components c0,c1,c2) which INFLATES its participation, so the intended OUTGROUP is chosen as the map-everything-onto root — opposite of the ground-truth expectation (DR = Vulgate outgroup). Screenshot 02-02-corpus-overview.png shows DR rendered as tree root.
findings.recommendation: Base root-completeness on multi-member (core/shell) participation only, excluding singleton components, so a heavily-fragmented outgroup is not rewarded for its gaps; or expose the singleton-adjusted participation alongside so the auto-suggestion reflects shared-content completeness.
findings.verify_reasoning:
Mechanical facts confirmed. Code counts ALL components including singletons for the root heuristic (actual paths core/palimpsest/corpus_graph.py:407-408 and core/palimpsest/analysis/phylo.py:24-30 — finding cited collections/ subdir, which is wrong). Live GET /api/collections/matthew-mark-6way/phyletic-tree returns suggested_root=DR-Mt with participation DR-Mt=5, Gen-Mt=3, KJV-Mt=2 — matches finding exactly. Corpus-graph shows DR-Mt's 5 = core1(c7)+shell1(c6)+singleton3(c0,c1,c2); summary "1 core·1 shell·6 singleton". Screenshot 02-02-corpus-overview.png confirms Root dropdown shows DR-Mt "(suggested)" and tree renders DR as root. So the described behavior is real and reproduced.

BUT the finding's central causal claim is refuted by direct recomputation. The claim is that singleton inflation is WHY DR is chosen, and that excluding singletons (the recommendation) would fix it. It would not: under multi-member (core+shell) participation DR-Mt=2 TIES Gen-Mt=2, and the deterministic lowest-index tie-break (key=(participation[i], -i), line 408) still selects DR-Mt because DR is member index 0 (first in project_ids order). Under core-only participation all six tie at 1 and DR-Mt still wins. I verified this numerically. The root selection is actually driven by collection member ordering + tie-break, not by singleton inflation — so the recommended remediation does not change the reported symptom.

Also, the "outgroup-as-root is wrong" framing overstates the defect. The docstring (corpus_graph.py:396-398, phylo.py:10-12) documents the root as an explicitly user-overridable "map everything onto X" reading lens over an UNROOTED neighbor-joining tree — not a phylogenetic ancestral-root claim; rooting is cosmetic and the UI exposes an override dropdown labeled "(suggested)". test_phylo.py/test_corpus_graph.py show singleton inclusion in participation is intentional and tested, not an oversight.

Residual legitimate concern (info/low): the raw participation count does reward a fragmented member, a mildly misleading "completeness" signal; the finding's secondary suggestion (expose singleton-adjusted participation) has UX merit. But there is no correctness bug, the value is user-overridable, and the blamed mechanism does not actually cause the observed root choice — high severity is unwarranted.

findings.title: Jaccard-over-components yields degenerate 0.0 distances and misclassifies cross-book pairs as near
findings.evidence: Live phyletic-tree distance matrix: Mark2(Gen)↔Mark3(KJV)=0.0 (branch_length 0.0, node0 children both bl=0.0). Reproduced via phylo.component_distance_matrix: both members appear in ONLY the single core (participation 1 each) → both=1, union=1, d=1-1/1=0.0 regardless of true text distance. Same degeneracy gives Matt3(KJV)↔Mark2(Gen)=0.5 — KJV-Matthew judged as close to Geneva-Mark as the genuinely near-identical Geneva/KJV pairs. Root cause is the 2-real-component distance structure (finding above); the NJ math itself (phylo.py) is correct.
findings.recommendation: Once the graph produces per-passage components (fix findings 1-2), the distances become non-degenerate. Additionally consider weighting Jaccard by component size/breadth so a single shared giant core cannot drive a 0.0 distance, and surface a warning when the distance matrix is built from < K non-singleton components (here only 2).
findings.verify_reasoning:
Every quantitative claim reproduces exactly against the live server (http://localhost:8092) and the code. I hit GET /api/collections/matthew-mark-6way/phyletic-tree and .../corpus-graph, and re-derived the matrix from phylo.component_distance_matrix (core/palimpsest/analysis/phylo.py:33-52) using the live component sets.

Live graph structure (confirmed via analyze_graph.py + UI badge "1 core / 1 shell / 6 singleton" in .scratch/audit6/screenshots/02-02-corpus-overview.png): 8 components = 6 singletons + 1 shell {DR-Mt,GV-Mt} + 1 core {all 6}. Only 2 non-singleton components, as claimed. The screenshot's ALL-PAIRS SHARED COMPONENTS grid shows every pair sharing exactly 1 component except DR-Mt/GV-Mt (2) — the mechanism the finding describes.

Distance matrix (live): GV-Mk<->KJV-Mk = 0.000 (each participation=1, both only in the single core; union=1+1-1=1; d=1-1/1=0) CONFIRMED. KJV-Mt<->GV-Mk = 0.500 CONFIRMED. Tree: node0's children GV-Mk and KJV-Mk both have branch_length 0.0 => cophenetic distance 0.0 CONFIRMED.

The finding is if anything UNDERSTATED: it says KJV-Mt is "as close" to Geneva-Mark as the near-identical Geneva/KJV sisters. Actually the matrix judges KJV-Mt<->GV-Mk (cross-BOOK, cross-translation, should be far) = 0.5, NEARER than KJV-Mt<->its true sister GV-Mt = 0.75. The full 15-pair ranking puts four 0.5 pairs (three cross-book) ahead of the genuine same-translation sisters at 0.75. Distances are content-blind — pure component-participation topology.

Root-cause attribution is correct and honestly scoped. phylo.py math is sound: tests pass (pytest tests/test_phylo.py, 6 passed), and my simulation with an IDEAL per-passage graph yields the right topology (sisters 0.083 vs cross-book 0.955). So the degeneracy is a downstream consequence of the upstream graph collapsing everything into one giant core, exactly as the finding states ("Root cause is the 2-real-component distance structure... the NJ math itself is correct"). Confirmed via grep that NO warning is emitted when the matrix is built from too few non-singleton components, so the recommended guard is genuinely absent.

Severity high is right: this is a shipped, user-facing phyletic tree (Corpus > Overview) producing demonstrably wrong stemma conclusions on the canonical validation collection, with no guard flagging the degeneracy. Not critical because it is a manifestation of the upstream graph defect (not an independent algorithmic bug), and the finding does not double-count it.

findings.title: Near-duplicate cluster detection misses the Geneva↔KJV Matthew pair that is as near-identical as the Mark pair
findings.evidence: GET :8092/.../corpus-analyses → near_duplicate_clusters=[[Mark2(Gen),Mark3(KJV)]] only. Matt2(Gen)↔Matt3(KJV) is NOT clustered because their component-Jaccard distance is 0.75 (Matt2 sits in shell c6, Matt3 does not) even though the two texts are textually as near-identical as the Mark pair. collections/corpus_graph.py:492 single_linkage_clusters over phylo_distance_rows inherits the degenerate component structure, so 'near-duplicate' reflects component co-membership, not actual text similarity.
findings.recommendation: Either derive near-duplicate clusters from a direct pairwise text/embedding similarity (the sweep or C2 scores) rather than component-Jaccard, or document that near-duplicate here means 'shares nearly all homology components' — which, given the coarse graph, is a much weaker signal than the UI label 'near-duplicate' implies.

findings.title: Cross-book edges appear as edges with no shell/weak-link distinction, so the graph cannot represent synoptic-but-not-identical relationships
findings.evidence: corpus_graph.py:283-293 treats all edges identically for union; the only classifications are core/shell/singleton by member-reach (lines 317-326). The 66 weak synoptic Mt↔Mk edges (scores 0.16–1.7) that legitimately indicate shared-content-different-wording have no representation other than forcing a full union. The design (corpus_graph.py:4-10) has no notion of a weighted/weak homology edge or a 'partial correspondence' class between shell and singleton.
findings.recommendation: Introduce edge weights into the component model and either (a) a minimum-weight union threshold, or (b) a distinct 'weak/synteny' edge class rendered separately in the block map, so genuine synoptic relationships are visible without collapsing distinct books.

findings.title: corpus_analyses recomputes the pangenome distance matrix independently of phyletic_tree (drift + wasted work)
findings.evidence: phyletic_tree calls phylo.component_distance_matrix (corpus_graph.py:406); corpus_analyses separately calls phylo_distance_rows → component_distance_matrix again (corpus_graph.py:491, 522-527) over the same graph. Two independent recomputations of the same matrix from the same components; if one call site's comp_set construction ever diverges (phyletic uses c.members sets, analyses uses idx lists) the tree and near-duplicate views could silently disagree.
findings.recommendation: Compute the distance matrix once per graph and share it between phyletic_tree, corpus_analyses, and single-linkage clustering to guarantee the tree and near-duplicate views are consistent and to avoid the O(components²) recompute.

findings.title: Phyletic tree leaf labels overlap/collide in the rendered SVG

findings.recommendation: Truncate/ellipsize leaf labels to a short display name (e.g. translation+book) with a title/tooltip for the full id, and offset labels to avoid same-y collisions.

dimensions.title: Documentation coherence & requirement traceability
dimensions.summary: The design corpus (Wave-0 vision/plan FR-1..22, Collections vision/plan FR-23..43, build journal, WALKTHROUGH, system-design, principles) is unusually rigorous: every FR I spot-checked maps to real, verifiable code and, for UI-facing FRs, to a live surface on :8092. The coherence problem is staleness, not fabrication: the two Wave-0 planning docs still carry "Draft for human review" status and near-universally unchecked done-criteria boxes even though the build journal + code prove P1-P9 and C1-C7 all shipped, embedded, and in-browser-proven (948 tests collected, baseline 947 GREEN). A handful of committed-code deviations (dispersion-as-endpoint not layer-track; FR-13 lanes living in the Analysis Suite Explore tab rather than "over the text" in the Browser OverviewBar) are honestly flagged in code comments but never back-propagated to the plan docs. The audit's own premise — that Phase-1 tracks are unwired in the UI — is refuted by the evidence.

The KJV verse-paragraph fix is verifiable on disk: KJV Matthew has exactly 1071 paragraph segments (tracks/segments.jsonl) matching its 1071 verses, and the live UI header reads '1071 paragraphs' — the fix holds and the substrate claim is grounded.

dimensions.title: Regression, gaps & latent-bug hunt
dimensions.summary: The KJV verse-paragraphing regression is genuinely fixed: the live 6-way collection shows Geneva↔KJV Matthew as 1071×1071 with one clean full-length diagonal (matrix metadata query_paragraphs=1071/target_paragraphs=1071; alignment records = single record q[15-1071]/t[15-1071] strand=+; dotplot screenshot shows a crisp corner-to-corner diagonal), DR fragments (39 records), cross-book Mt↔Mk gives weak short fragments (18 records), and the pangenome is exactly 1 core / 1 shell / 6 singleton. The code is mature and defensive against silent caps (smith_waterman default max_alignments=None + WARNING on truncation; candidate_gen empirical-recall with force-exhaustive escape; embedding_track _PAIRWISE_CAP returns None not silent-drop). However there is one confirmed latent crash (RQA UnboundLocalError on <2 paragraphs, untested), and the downstream pangenome/near-dup/phyletic-tree pipeline does NOT robustly recover the collection's core same-versification signal — Geneva↔KJV is caught for Mark (near-dup, tree distance 0.0) but MISSED for Matthew (tree distance 0.75, absent from near_duplicate_clusters) despite an identical clean diagonal, plus the edition-diff and the Compare-tab default-method UX produce misleading outputs.
strengths: KJV verse-paragraphing fix verified end-to-end: /api/alignment/{Gv-Mt}/{KJV-Mt}/matrix reports query_paragraphs=1071, target_paragraphs=1071, and /records returns exactly one full-length forward diagonal (q[15-1071] t[15-1071], identity 0.746); dotplot screenshot 07-compare-dotplot.png shows a single crisp main diagonal on the 1071x1071 cross-similarity heatmap — the prior chapter-level-paragraph zeroing regression is gone.

Ground-truth biology analogy holds on the live substrate: DR (different versification) fragments into 39 short alignment records vs Geneva (smith_waterman.py extraction), cross-book Geneva-Mt vs Geneva-Mk yields 18 weak short fragments (synoptic-but-not-wording), and /corpus-graph summary is exactly {core:1, shell:1, singleton:6} = 8 components as specified.

Genuinely anti-silent-cap engineering: alignment/smith_waterman.py:52-55 defaults max_alignments=None (exhaustive) and logs at WARNING on truncation (never silent); analysis/candidate_gen.py:10-12 documents empirical recall with a force_exhaustive escape; tracks/embedding_track.py:41-46 returns None (not a fabricated stat) above _PAIRWISE_CAP=800.

self_similarity.py:1155-1168 uses a stage-then-atomic-os.replace commit with an except BaseException rollback that unlinks every staged temp and re-raises, so filename-scanning readers never observe an orphan .bin or a manifest without its data — correct crash-safety.

All 6 members are cosine-congruent on the live server (/congruence: all_congruent=true, one embedding group, missing=[]), confirming the MLX Qwen3-Embedding-4B substrate is intact and the embedding projection view renders (08-analysis-representations.png, 237 chunks).

findings.title: RQATrack.extract() raises UnboundLocalError for any text with <2 paragraphs (state_source referenced but never assigned)
findings.evidence: core/palimpsest/tracks/rqa.py:160-161 (if len(paras)<2: metrics=zeros, else-branch skipped) then :200 source=f"rqa_{state_source}/0.1" and :210 reference state_source, which is only assigned at :167 inside the else-branch. Confirmed in committed HEAD via `git show HEAD:.../rqa.py`. Reproduced: simulating the control flow raises `UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'state_source'`.
findings.recommendation: Initialize state_source="tfidf" (or "none") before the `if len(paras)<2` guard at rqa.py:159, so the manifest source/metadata are well-defined for degenerate single-paragraph inputs. Add a test with a 0/1-paragraph project (tests/test_signals.py RQA class currently only exercises small_project with >=2 paras, so this branch has zero coverage).
findings.verify_reasoning:
Every technical claim verified by direct code read, git HEAD comparison, and live reproduction against the real code.

CODE (core/palimpsest/tracks/rqa.py): Line 160-161 `if len(paras) < 2:` sets `metrics = np.zeros((1,3))` and skips the else. `state_source` is assigned ONLY inside the else branch — at line 167 (`= "tfidf"`) and line 177 (`= "embeddings"`). It is then referenced unconditionally at line 200 (`source=f"rqa_{state_source}/0.1"`) and line 210 (`"state_vector_source": state_source`). grep confirms those are the only 5 occurrences. `git show HEAD:.../rqa.py | grep` shows identical line numbers, so committed HEAD == working tree.

REPRODUCTION: Two ways. (1) Faithful control-flow simulation raises `UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'state_source' where it is not associated with a value`. (2) More conclusively, I drove the REAL, unmodified `RQATrack().extract()` against a project whose `paragraphs()` returns a single tuple — it raised the exact same UnboundLocalError through the production code path, not a mock of it.

REACHABILITY: `project.paragraphs()` (project.py:225) returns whatever `segment_paragraphs()` yields from the reference text with no lower-bound enforcement, so a single/empty-paragraph subtext reaches the buggy branch. Notably the `<2` guard was added deliberately to handle degenerate input gracefully (compare topics.py:61-63, which raises a clean ValueError for the same condition) — but the state_source leak defeats that intent. RQA is registered in TrackRegistry and run by runner.py in the standard pipeline, so ingesting any <2-paragraph project crashes signal extraction.

TEST GAP: Confirmed. The `small_project` fixture (test_signals.py:45) has `paragraph_count: 5`; all TestRQA tests use it, so the `<2` branch has zero coverage. The recommended fix (initialize `state_source` before the guard, add a 0/1-paragraph test) is correct and minimal.

SEVERITY ADJUSTMENT: Reported as high; I lower to medium. It is a real, reproducible, uncovered latent bug and worth fixing, but the trigger (a project with <2 paragraphs) is an uncommon edge case — real subtexts like the Matt/Mark biblical books have many paragraphs. It fails loud (a clean crash, not silent bad data or wrong output on typical inputs), affects no mainline path, and the fix is one line. That profile is medium, not high.

findings.title: Near-duplicate detection MISSES Geneva-KJV Matthew while catching Geneva-KJV Mark, despite identical clean diagonals — same-versification signal not robustly recovered
findings.evidence: /collections/matthew-mark-6way/corpus-analyses returns near_duplicate_clusters=[{members:[Gv-Mk,KJV-Mk],size:2}] ONLY. But /alignment/{Gv-Mt}/{KJV-Mt}/records is a single full diagonal (identity 0.746) and /alignment/{Gv-Mk}/{KJV-Mk}/records is a single full diagonal (identity 0.706) — equally clean. Near-dup uses single_linkage over the pangenome Jaccard matrix (analysis/corpus_analysis.py:92-109) with duplicate_threshold=0.15 (server.py:2459); phyletic-tree distances give Gv-Mk↔KJV-Mk=0.000 but Gv-Mt↔KJV-Mt=0.750.
findings.recommendation: The collection's central ground-truth (Geneva↔KJV near-identical) is only half-recovered. Root cause: _merge_intervals in corpus_graph.py:267 collapses all overlapping Matthew alignments (DR-Mt/Gv-Mt/KJV-Mt all cover ~[15-1071]) into one core anchor, so the single Gv-Mt↔KJV-Mt edge (node n5↔n6) is absorbed and never forms a distinct shell/near-dup component. Consider deriving near-dup from alignment identity/coverage directly rather than from the coarse pangenome-participation Jaccard, or split anchors when a pair's mutual identity greatly exceeds a third member's.
findings.verify_reasoning: Every factual claim verified against live API and source. (1) GET /api/collections/matthew-mark-6way/corpus-analyses returns near_duplicate_clusters=[{Gv-Mk,KJV-Mk} size 2] ONLY; Gv-Mt/KJV-Mt not clustered. (2) /api/alignment/{Gv-Mt}/{KJV-Mt}/records = single full diagonal queryStart15 queryEnd1071 identity 0.7458; /api/alignment/{Gv-Mk}/{KJV-Mk}/records = single full diagonal [0,678] identity 0.7063 — both equally clean single diagonals, Matthew identity actually HIGHER. (3) phyletic-tree distances: Gv-Mk↔KJV-Mk=0.000, Gv-Mt↔KJV-Mt=0.750 exactly as claimed. (4) Code path confirmed: server.py:2459 duplicate_threshold=0.15 → corpus_graph.corpus_analyses:491-492 phylo_distance_rows→component_distance_matrix (pangenome participation Jaccard) → single_linkage_clusters; identity is NEVER used in the near-dup/phylo path (grepped corpus_analysis.py/corpus_graph.py/phylo.py — no 'identity'). (5) Root-cause mechanism verified by inspecting the live corpus-graph: _merge_intervals (corpus_graph.py:123,267) merges each member's overlapping alignments into anchors, and union-find collapses Gv-Mt(n5) and KJV-Mt(n6) — the very nodes the finding names — into one 'core' component c7 that contains ALL 6 members' Matthew AND Mark anchors. So the Gv-Mt↔KJV-Mt sister edge is absorbed; per-member participation sets are DR-Mt{c0,c1,c2,c6,c7} Gv-Mt{c3,c6,c7} KJV-Mt{c4,c7} Gv-Mk{c7} KJV-Mk{c7}, giving Jaccard-dist Gv-Mt↔KJV-Mt=0.75 vs Gv-Mk↔KJV-Mk=0.0 (reproduced by hand, matches phyletic output). Severity-STRENGTHENING evidence: I swept duplicate_threshold live (0.15/0.5/0.75/0.8) — no value recovers the sisters as a distinct pair; 0.5 yields a cross-book FALSE POSITIVE (KJV-Mt with DR-Mk/Gv-Mk/KJV-Mk) while still missing Gv-Mt, and 0.75 collapses all six. The mechanism is structurally unable to recover the collection's central ground truth for Matthew, not merely mistuned. One minor imprecision in the finding's framing: Mark's sisters cluster not because they were 'spared' merging (they too are fully in c7) but because neither Mark sister carries any distinguishing singleton/shell component, whereas DR-Mt's idiosyncratic unaligned gaps spawned singletons c0/c1/c2 + shell c6 that broke the Matthew sisters' participation-set symmetry — the absorption-into-core diagnosis and the n5↔n6 citation are nonetheless correct. This nuance does not change the conclusion or the recommended fix (derive near-dup from alignment identity/coverage directly). Severity 'high' is appropriate but sits at the high/medium boundary: it is an analysis-quality/correctness defect that half-defeats a headline collection feature and cannot be tuned away, though it is not a crash/data-loss and the correct sister signal remains visible in the phyletic tree (Mk-sisters 0.0) and raw alignment identities.

findings.title: Phyletic tree distance is pangenome-participation Jaccard, not sequence similarity — quantized to ~6 values and inverts the true kinship on this collection
findings.evidence: analysis/phylo.py:33-52 component_distance_matrix = 1 - |comps with both| / |comps with either|. /phyletic-tree distances take only {0.0,0.5,0.667,0.75,0.8,0.833}; Gv-Mt↔KJV-Mt=0.750 is LARGER (more distant) than DR-Mt↔Gv-Mt=0.667, contradicting the spec that Geneva↔KJV (same versification) should be tightest and DR the outgroup.
findings.recommendation: With only 8 components (1 core all-6, 1 shell 2-member, 6 singletons) the Jaccard distance is near-degenerate and cannot express fine kinship. Document this limitation prominently in the phyletic-tree view, or offer an alternative distance (mean alignment identity / 1-coverage) so the tree recovers the designed Vulgate-outgroup / Geneva-KJV-sister topology.

findings.title: Edition-diff summary reports 0 unchanged / 1071 replacements for a near-identical translation pair — exact string equality makes 'unchanged' effectively unreachable
findings.evidence: /alignment/{Gv-Mt}/{KJV-Mt}/diff summary={insertions:0, deletions:0, replacements:1071, unchanged:0}. compute_edition_diff (alignment/edition_diff.py:91) runs difflib.SequenceMatcher over element-wise paragraph text (exact hashes); any single-char delta ⇒ 'replace'. Screenshot 07-compare-diff.png shows verse 1 differing only by one comma yet flagged 'Changed', header '0 added · 0 removed · 1071 changed · 0 unchanged'.
findings.recommendation: For cross-translation use the summary is uninformative (every verse is 'changed' by construction). Add a similarity-graded classification (e.g. 'minor' vs 'substantive' via char-level ratio or token Jaccard) so the summary distinguishes a one-comma diff from a rewrite. Also note text_a/text_b are silently truncated at [:500] chars (edition_diff.py:117) — long verses are clipped in the record.

findings.title: Compare tab defaults to Semantic (SBERT) and shows 'Ready to align'/'No alignment records' even though a clean word_overlap alignment exists on disk
findings.evidence: Screenshots 07-compare-alignment.png and 07-compare-synteny.png show 'Ready to align — Select a method and click Align' and 'No alignment records. Run alignment first to see synteny ribbons' with method dropdown = 'Semantic (SBERT)'. Yet /alignment/{Gv-Mt}/{KJV-Mt}/status=completed and /records returns 1 clean diagonal (method='word'). The dotplot's cross-similarity heatmap (07-compare-dotplot.png) DOES render because it reads the stored matrix directly.
findings.recommendation: Default the Compare method selector to whatever pre-computed alignment/comparison already exists for the pair (or auto-load it), so Alignment/Synteny/Diff don't present false 'no alignment' empty states when a completed word_overlap alignment is on disk. A user would otherwise conclude no alignment exists.

findings.title: Same shell component is classified 'shell' by corpus-graph but 'singleton' by the diffusion histogram (bin boundary excludes 2/6=0.333)
findings.evidence: /corpus-graph summary: {core:1, shell:1, singleton:6}. /corpus-analyses diffusion.component_spread_histogram: {singleton:7, narrow:0, broad:0, core:1}. _spread_histogram (corpus_graph.py:530-542) bins spread<0.34 as 'singleton'; a 2-of-6-member shell has spread 0.333 < 0.34, so the shell is miscounted as a 7th singleton.
findings.recommendation: Align the histogram bands with the component classification (shell = >1 and <all members), e.g. lower the narrow band boundary below 2/n or bin by member-count rather than fraction, so the two endpoints agree on the same graph.

findings.title: Pangenome/near-dup pipeline has thin unit coverage; phylo has one test file and the coarse-distance / classification-mismatch behaviors are unguarded
findings.evidence: tests/: phylo referenced by 1 file (test_phylo.py); collections_sweep/probe/masking each 1 file; corpus_graph 3 files. No test asserts near_duplicate_clusters symmetry across near-identical pairs, nor the diffusion-histogram vs component-classification consistency. RQA extract tests (test_signals.py:130-155) never hit the <2-paragraph branch.
findings.recommendation: Add regression tests: (1) RQA extract on a 0/1-paragraph project; (2) a synthetic pangenome where two members are near-identical, asserting they land in the same near-dup cluster AND the smallest tree distance; (3) assert corpus-graph shell count == diffusion histogram non-singleton/non-core count.

dimensions.title: Collection workbench UI (6-way Corpus tab)
dimensions.summary: The collection workbench is a genuinely mature, honest 7-sub-tab surface: all views render real data (no stubs, no error/empty/runFirst flags across the Corpus tab per evidence.json 02-02..02-08), the KJV verse-paragraph fix is verified (all 6 members now report 1071/678 paras vs the old 131/69), the congruence contract is correctly satisfied (API all_congruent:true, badge shows "congruent · cosine"), the Probe returns methodologically correct cross-translation retrieval, and the Sweep per-pair table faithfully recovers the ground-truth pair ranking. The dominant weakness is scholarly legibility: the six members are near-identical raw slugs truncated to indistinguishable prefixes in EVERY view (block map, matrix, tree, members, probe, sweep), so a scholar cannot tell Matthew from Mark or DR from Geneva from KJV without hovering. Secondarily, the corpus-graph homology layer is so coarse (16 nodes, 1 core + 1 shell component over whole-book blocks) that the Overview/Masking surfaces cannot expose the versification-drift signal the collection was built to exercise — that signal lives only in the finer Sweep/Probe/Compare layers.
strengths: Probe is correct and valuable: a ref probe on DR-Matt chunk5 (Magi/Herod) returns KJV-Matt (sim 0.9587) and Geneva-Matt (0.9416) as top cross-translation matches over the shared 2560-dim embedding space, all 6 members searched (POST /api/collections/matthew-mark-6way/probe; evidence.json 06-probe-result interaction.ranProbe:true) — real semantic retrieval, not word overlap.

Sweep per-pair table honestly recovers the ground truth: same-book cross-translation pairs score highest recall (Gen-Mat<->KJV-Mat 24%, Gen-Mrk<->KJV-Mrk 23%) while cross-book synoptic pairs score lowest (Gen-Mat<->KJV-Mrk 2%), and null recall is rendered 'n/a' not fabricated (sweep.ts:72; GET /api/collections/.../sweep/8a555cc5f398). findings.title: Member labels are indistinguishable raw slugs in every workbench view — a scholar cannot tell the 6 members apart
findings.evidence: screenshot 02-02-corpus-overview.png (block-map rows 'douay-rheims-bib...', '1599-geneva-bible...', 'the-holy-bible-kin...' each appear twice, identical); CorpusView.tsx:70 (w-28 truncate), :105 (max-w-24 truncate), MembersPanel.tsx:109 (max-w-52 truncate), ProbePanel.tsx:190 (renders r.project_id)
findings.recommendation: Resolve member ids to their friendly work titles (the Home page already knows them: 'Douay-Rheims -- Matthew', 'King James -- Mark', etc. per evidence.json 01-landing headings). Thread a member->label map (from /api/collections or /api/projects) into CorpusView/MembersPanel/ProbePanel/SweepPanel and render the label with the slug in the title/tooltip, not the reverse.
findings.verify_reasoning:
CONFIRMED, severity high. Every code claim holds at the real paths (finding cited a flat CorpusView.tsx; actual files live under browser/src/components/CorpusView/, but the line numbers and content match): BlockMap renders {lane.member} raw in `w-28 shrink-0 truncate` (CorpusView.tsx:70); AllPairsMatrix renders {rowM} in `max-w-24 truncate` (CorpusView.tsx:105) and the bottom axis renders {m.slice(0,4)} (CorpusView.tsx:136) — literally 'doua','1599','the-'; MembersPanel renders {m} in `truncate max-w-52` (MembersPanel.tsx:109/111); ProbePanel renders {r.project_id} in `truncate max-w-40` (ProbePanel.tsx:190) and the member dropdown renders raw {m} (:112). SweepPanel routes through shortMember() (sweep.ts:88 -> e.g. '1599-genev…ok-mark'), slug-based too. Even the hover tooltips carry only the slug (title={lane.member} at :69/:213, title={rowM} at :105/:115), so hovering does not disambiguate.

Visual confirmation: screenshot 02-02-corpus-overview.png shows the block-map lanes as three pairs of identical-looking truncated slugs (douay-rheims-bib..., 1599-geneva-bible..., the-holy-bible-kin... — each appearing twice, rows 1&4/2&5/3&6), the all-pairs matrix axis as doua/1599/the-, and the phyletic tree with the same truncated slugs. screenshot 02-03-corpus-members.png shows the Members table Member column as the same 3 duplicated truncated slugs, the Work column empty (—, work_id null), and only a second giant slug in Lineage to tell Matthew from Mark. A scholar genuinely cannot distinguish DR-Matthew (row1) from DR-Mark (row4).

Fix is real and grounded: GET /api/projects (hit live at :8092) returns per-project `title` that fully disambiguates all 6 — 'Douay-Rheims -- Matthew' / 'Douay-Rheims -- Mark' / '1599 Geneva -- Matthew' / '1599 Geneva -- Mark' / 'King James -- Matthew' / 'King James -- Mark' (chapter-in-book-0047 vs 0048; chapter-in-book-matthew vs mark). The Home page already renders these exact titles (evidence.json 01-landing headings, lines 37-45). Grep confirms NO component in browser/src/components/CorpusView/ fetches /api/projects or builds any member->title map — the whole workbench is blind to labels the app already has.

Two corrections to the finding (wording, not substance): (1) the recommended source '/api/collections' does NOT carry per-member titles — verified the payload has only a collection-level `label` plus raw project_ids; the correct source is /api/projects (.title). (2) ProbePanel's ProbeResult.label field is NOT a friendly title — a read-only ref-probe returned label='093983a081e20ead' (a chunk/layer hash), so the code's use of r.project_id over r.label is actually correct; the real fix is joining project_id against /api/projects titles.

Strengths worth recording: the underlying data is methodologically sound — the ref-probe on DR-Matthew chunk 0 self-matches at similarity 1.0 and surfaces KJV cross-translation at 0.977/0.893 (embeddings correctly detect near-identical same-content across translations); congruence report shows all 6 members in one embedding space (all_congruent=true, evidence.json 03-congruence); pangenome summary reads 1 core / 1 shell / 6 singleton as designed. The defect is purely presentational, but it defeats the stated purpose of a 6-way cross-translation workbench, so high (misleading/unreadable output in a core interpretive flow) is the right severity — not critical (no data corruption; a slug is technically present), not medium (this is the primary way a user identifies which text a lane/row/probe-hit belongs to).

findings.title: AllPairsMatrix column headers collapse to 4-char prefixes ('doua 1599 the- doua 1599 the-') — the axis is unreadable and duplicated
findings.evidence: CorpusView.tsx:136 renders `{m.slice(0, 4)}` for every column header; screenshot 02-02 bottom axis shows 'doua 1599 the- doua 1599 the-' with two identical triples

findings.verify_reasoning:
CONFIRMED at the cited file:line. CorpusView/CorpusView.tsx:136 renders `{m.slice(0, 4)}` for every column header (title={m}, max-w-8 truncate). I verified what `m` actually is by GETting the live graph: http://localhost:8092/api/collections/matthew-mark-6way/corpus-graph returns members = the raw project-id slugs in order [douay...-0047, 1599-geneva...-matthew, the-holy-bible-king...-matthew, douay...-0048, 1599-geneva...-mark, the-holy-bible-king...-mark]. slice(0,4) of these yields exactly: doua, 1599, the-, doua, 1599, the-. Screenshot .scratch/audit6/screenshots/02-02-corpus-overview.png shows the ALL-PAIRS SHARED COMPONENTS matrix bottom axis literally reading `doua 1599 the- doua 1599 the-` — six columns, three distinct labels, so columns 1&4 (both DR), 2&5 (both Geneva), 3&6 (both KJV) are pixel-identical. A scholar cannot tell Matthew-column from Mark-column. Matrix VALUES are correct (Geneva↔KJV Matthew = 2, all else = 1), so this is a labeling/encoding defect, not data corruption.

The finding's mechanism and EVIDENCE are accurate; its only imprecision is the shorthand 'Matt1/Matt2/Matt3...' — the real member strings are full slugs (douay-.../1599-.../the-...), not those short tokens, but the auditor's quoted prefixes ('doua 1599 the-') are exactly right. If anything the finding is slightly UNDER-scoped: the same never-resolve-a-title defect pervades the whole view. Row labels at line 105 render full `rowM` with CSS `truncate max-w-24`, so rows 1&4/2&5/3&6 show identical truncated translation prefixes and cannot distinguish Matthew from Mark either (visible in screenshot). BlockMap (line 72, `{lane.member}` w-28 truncate) has the same problem — rows 1-3 and 4-6 show identical labels. Nowhere in CorpusView is a human title resolved, despite the app header rendering 'Douay-Rheims -- Matthew' (a resolver exists elsewhere). The recommended fix is feasible: translation is in the slug prefix and book is recoverable from the suffix (DR uses -0047/-0048, Geneva/KJV use -matthew/-mark), so a label like 'DR-Mt','Gn-Mt','KJV-Mt','DR-Mk',... is derivable.

Severity: keep HIGH. Per rubric high = misleading output on a core flow. The all-pairs matrix is the flagship comparison surface of the flagship 6-way validation collection, and its column axis is genuinely unreadable and duplicated. It is not critical (values correct, no false analysis, hover title is a poor escape hatch), and it is arguably borderline medium since it is pure labeling — but because it degrades the primary interpretive surface AND the same failure recurs across block map and matrix rows, high is honest. Grounded=true: I read the code, hit the live API, and viewed the screenshot.
