dimensions.title: Compare / pairwise-visualization UI
dimensions.summary: The Compare tab's five sub-views split cleanly into "works" and "broken-on-load." Diff is excellent and directly validates the verse-paragraph fix (1071 vs 1071 verse-aligned pairs, correct near-identical Geneva-vs-KJV punctuation/spelling diffs). The Dotplot faithfully renders the single giant main diagonal the data actually contains (verified: main-diagonal cosine-band mean 0.741 vs off-diagonal 0.066; 1012/1043 high cells on the main diagonal). But three views (Synteny, Circos, Alignment) render empty or ribbon-less because persisted alignment records are never auto-loaded on mount/tab-switch — they only appear after manually clicking "Align," even though the record already exists on disk (GET /api/alignment/.../records returns 1 record). Two honesty gaps compound this: the Dotplot has no color legend, and the underlying matrix is word_overlap, not the collection's MLX cosine embeddings that the validation set was built to exercise. Diff silently truncates to 500 of 1071 changed verses.
strengths: Diff view is the standout: 07-compare-diff.png shows correct side-by-side verse-aligned comparison (A:¶0/B:¶0 ... 1071 changed, 0 added/removed), directly confirming the KJV verse-paragraphing fix holds (1071==1071 paragraphs, DiffView.tsx summary bar). Encoding is honest: red=A/green=B, colored legend swatches with matching counts (DiffView.tsx:76-90).

The Dotplot honestly renders the ground-truth signal: 07-compare-dotplot.png shows one clean full-length main diagonal for the near-identical pair, matching the matrix data (main-diag mean 0.741, off-diag 0.066, 1012/1043 cells>0.5 on the ±2 main diagonal). No fabricated structure; the apparent 'anti-diagonal' is a low-res thumbnail moiré, not real data.

ComparativeDotplot color mapping is correct for its data: interpolateColor clamps to [0,1] (ComparativeDotplot.tsx:17) and the word_overlap matrix genuinely ranges [0,1] (verified min 0.0 max 1.0, zero negatives), so there is no cosine [-1,1] mislabel for this matrix. Hover readout shows the real cell value to 3 decimals (ComparativeDotplot.tsx:218-221).

Empty-state copy is specific and honest per view rather than generic: Synteny says 'No alignment records. Run alignment first to see synteny ribbons.' (SyntenyView.tsx:117), Alignment says 'Run alignment from the toolbar above.' (AlignmentView.tsx:138), Dotplot says 'Run a semantic alignment first to generate the matrix.' (ComparativeDotplot.tsx:206).

Interaction affordances are genuinely wired where data exists: Dotplot has working wheel-zoom + clampViewport + hover crosshair (ComparativeDotplot.tsx:171-199); Circos/Synteny ribbons have hover-highlight and Circos ribbons click through to the Alignment view (CircosView.tsx:104-107,214).

findings.title: Synteny, Circos and Alignment show no data on load despite a persisted alignment record existing
findings.evidence: SyntenyView 07-compare-synteny.png (blank + 'No alignment records'); CircosView 07-compare-circos.png (two rings, ZERO ribbons); vs GET http://localhost:8092/api/alignment/<Geneva-Matt>/<KJV-Matt>/records → returns 1 record (queryStart 15→1071, identity 0.746, status 'completed'). comparisonStore.ts:150-159 loadAlignmentResults is only invoked from runAlignment's poll (line 113); nothing calls it on mount/tab-switch, so alignmentRecords stays [] and SyntenyView.tsx:114 / CircosView.tsx:193 / AlignmentView.tsx:135 all short-circuit to empty.
findings.recommendation: On CompareView mount (and when secondaryProjectId changes), call loadAlignmentResults(activeProjectId, secondaryProjectId) to hydrate persisted records — mirroring ComparativeDotplot's auto loadCrossMatrix useEffect (ComparativeDotplot.tsx:59-63). Then Synteny/Circos/Alignment reflect existing results without forcing a redundant re-Align.
findings.verify_reasoning:
Confirmed the mechanism, the evidence, and the fix by reading the code, hitting the live API, and viewing the screenshots.

MECHANISM (code): comparisonStore.ts:150-159 loadAlignmentResults is invoked from exactly one place — runAlignment's completion poll (line 113). Nothing else calls it. CompareView.tsx has NO useEffect at all for hydrating records; the only mount-time trigger when a target is chosen, projectStore.ts:249-264 loadSecondaryProject, loads only the project text and sets secondaryProjectId — it never calls loadAlignmentResults or loadCrossMatrix. So alignmentRecords stays [] until the user clicks Align. The three views short-circuit on that empty array: SyntenyView.tsx:114 (early return 'No alignment records'), AlignmentView.tsx:135 (early return 'No alignment records. Run alignment from the toolbar'), CircosView.tsx:193 (records.map produces zero ribbons). Additionally CompareView.tsx:259 gates AlignmentView behind alignmentRecords.length>0, and CompareView.tsx:233 renders a 'Ready to align' placeholder whenever records is empty.

API (live :8092, read-only GET): /api/alignment/<Geneva-Matt>/<KJV-Matt>/records returns exactly 1 completed record (queryStart 15, queryEnd 1071, score 519.17, identity 0.7458, method 'word', strand '+'); /status returns {"status":"completed"}. So persisted data provably exists server-side.

SCREENSHOTS (Geneva-Matt vs KJV-Matt, the pair with the persisted record): 07-compare-synteny.png = blank canvas + 'No alignment records. Run alignment first to see synteny ribbons' + 'Ready to align' banner. 07-compare-circos.png = two concentric rings (Geneva blue outer, KJV orange inner) with ZERO connecting ribbons, despite the record spanning 15->1071. 07-compare-alignment.png = only the 'Ready to align / Select a method and click Align' placeholder (AlignmentView never mounts). Exactly matches the finding.

SCOPING NUANCE (does not lower verdict): the Dotplot is a partial exception — ComparativeDotplot.tsx:59-63 DOES auto-load loadCrossMatrix, so 07-compare-dotplot.png shows a real 1071x1071 heatmap with a clean full-length diagonal (methodologically correct for the near-identical same-versification Geneva<->KJV pair). But even the dotplot still shows the redundant 'Ready to align' placeholder above it and lacks its records-diagonal overlay, because that overlay also reads alignmentRecords (ComparativeDotplot.tsx:35,53-57). The finding's own wording ('two rings, ZERO ribbons' for Circos) is accurate rather than overstated.

FIX is correct and minimal: add a useEffect in CompareView keyed on (activeProjectId, secondaryProjectId) calling loadAlignmentResults(activeProjectId, secondaryProjectId), exactly mirroring ComparativeDotplot's existing loadCrossMatrix effect. This would hydrate persisted results on tab-switch/mount without forcing a redundant re-Align. One caveat worth adding: loadAlignmentResults (line 156-157) writes the fetch failure into `error`, which CompareView.tsx:214 renders as a red banner — so an auto-hydrate on a pair with no prior alignment would spuriously show an error unless the 404/no-results case is treated as empty rather than error.

Severity: HIGH is right — a broken core flow that presents misleading/false output (app asserts 'No alignment records' and 'Ready to align' while completed alignment data exists on the server), silently hiding real scholarly results from anyone returning to a comparison. Not critical: no data corruption, and it is recoverable by clicking Align.

findings.title: Dotplot has no color-scale legend/colorbar — a scholar cannot read what a shade means

findings.title: Cross-similarity matrix is word_overlap, not the collection's cosine embeddings — undersells the validation signal

findings.title: Dotplot hides low-similarity cells (value<0.1) and axis labels use a CSS var as canvas fillStyle

dimensions.title: Analysis suite UI (single-text, on KJV Matthew)
dimensions.summary: The Analysis tab on Matt3 (KJV Matthew) is a genuinely working, honest analysis suite, not a stub. The Tracks table correctly enumerates 19 producers with accurate status (2 computed, 17 pending, matching live /analysis/status), evidence levels, dependency gating, and real Details/Compute/Re-run affordances. Representations renders a real 237-point PCA scatter of the 2560-dim Qwen3 vectors (numpy SVD, deterministic), Explore renders two real lanes (chunk-band + embedding nn-density lane with 203 unique values), and the per-layer stats panel exposes a rich, methodologically-correct set of embedding views (pairwise/NN histograms, cosine heatmap correctly mapped [-1,1]->[0,1], k-means clusters). Profile honestly shows an empty-state (profile.json genuinely 404) with a clear description of what to run. The main gaps are: (1) many runnable tracks (narrative_arc, rqa, repeats, and all annotation tracks) produce NO rendered output anywhere in the Analysis tab because only 4 layer_keyed tracks surface as lanes; (2) the scatter and lanes are non-interactive (no hover/zoom/click-through to text) and lack axes/legend, limiting a scholar's ability to navigate results; (3) minor label/encoding honesty gaps.
strengths: Tracks table is truthful and complete: live GET /api/projects/<Matt3>/analysis/status returns exactly 19 tracks with 2 computed (chunking, embedding) and 17 pending, matching the UI header '2 computed · 17 pending · 0 running · 2 layers' (08-analysis-tracks.png; evidence.json 08-analysis-tracks textSample). Status icons, evidence levels (E1/E4/E5), dependency chips with unmet-dep gating (AnalysisPanel.tsx:805-808, 894), and per-track Compute/Re-run/Details are all wired.

Screenshot 08-analysis-representations.png shows a populated scatter with visible cluster structure, and evidence.json labels it 'embedding 87da3afb423732be projection scatter, 237 points'.

findings.title: Runnable signal tracks (narrative_arc, rqa, repeats) produce no rendered output anywhere in the Analysis tab

In 08-analysis-tracks.png these are all listed with a working 'Compute' button, but running e.g. narrative_arc or rqa flips the row to a green check with zero visible result in any Analysis sub-tab.

findings.verify_reasoning:
The finding's core code mechanism is accurate and grounded, but its scope is badly overstated — it conflates three distinct render pathways and is wrong on several named tracks.

VERIFIED MECHANISM (accurate): collectLayers (browser/src/components/AnalysisPanel/layers/types.ts:56-64) iterates `t.layers ?? []` and skips any track row lacking a `layers` key. server.py:1130 nests `layers` only when `getattr(ext, "layer_keyed", False)` is true. Only 4 tracks set layer_keyed=True (chunking_track.py:79, repeat_track.py:40, embedding_track.py, repeat_mask_track.py). Live API confirms: GET /api/projects/<KJV-Matt>/analysis/status returns 19 tracks, exactly 4 with a `layers` field, 15 without. LayerWorkbench (Explore, LayerWorkbench.tsx:15,41) and EmbeddingScatter (Representations, AnalysisPanel.tsx:702,1036) render ONLY from collectLayers, so non-layer tracks never appear in Explore/Representations. Screenshot 08-analysis-explore.png shows only chunking+embedding lanes; 08-analysis-tracks.png shows narrative_arc/rqa/profile with live Compute buttons. LayerLane.test.tsx:55 documents non-layer tracks "contribute nothing" BY DESIGN.

WHERE THE FINDING IS WRONG (overstated):
1. TITLE names `repeats` as producing no output — FALSE. repeat_track.py:40 sets layer_keyed=True with track_view "repeat-band" (line 121); it renders as a band lane in Explore. The finding's own evidence body lists repeats among the 4 layer-keyed tracks, contradicting its title.
2. `profile` ("profile-signal") — HAS a dedicated renderer: the Analysis→Profile sub-tab (ProfileDashboard.tsx fetches signals/profile.json). Screenshot 08-analysis-profile.png shows a proper empty-state with CTA "Run the profile track to produce text-level statistics." Not a dead-end.
3. `lithmm`, `compartments`, `boundary_detection` are ANNOTATION tracks (output_type="annotation", verified per-track), rendered as annotation overlays in Reading/Browser (AnnotationOverlay.tsx:27-29 maps LitHMMAnnotation→lithmm, CompartmentAnnotation/DomainAnnotation→compartments). Their design target is the reading views, not Explore. Lumping them into "signal tracks producing no output" is a category error. (Aside: boundary_detection emits palimpsest:TextDomainAnnotation/TextBoundaryAnnotation which are absent from BODY_TYPE_TO_TRACK — a separate, real overlay-mapping gap, not this finding.)
4. `self_similarity` and `alphabet` are signal tracks consumed in the Compare tab (DotplotView.tsx, CompareView.tsx). Not Analysis-tab dead-ends, and not "no rendered output anywhere."

WHERE THE FINDING IS RIGHT (real but narrow): narrative_arc and rqa are the ONLY tracks that genuinely dead-end. grep across browser/src shows their signal files (signals/narrative_arc.json, signals/rqa.json) are NEVER fetched by any component — they appear only as a color in trackColors.ts:8,11 and description strings in AnalysisPanel.tsx:149,153. Clicking Compute produces a file nothing reads, flipping the row to a green check with zero rendered artifact anywhere in the app. This is a genuine honesty/dead-end gap, and the recommendation (inline "view in…" hint or add an Explore summary card) is valid — for these 2 tracks, not the 8 the finding claims.

SEVERITY: The real defect is 2 runnable actions with no consumable result — a UX/disclosure gap, not wrong/misleading output, data corruption, or a broken core flow. High → medium.

dimensions.title: Text views & navigation UI (reading/browser/texthic/landing)
dimensions.summary: The text-facing views are a mature, largely honest reading/navigation stack: the Reading view renders real verse text with a genuine multi-coordinate navigation toolbar (paragraph/char/section stepping, jump-to, zoom, section+track side panels), the Browser renders real structure/content tracks reflecting the recent verse-paragraphing fix (KJV Matthew now 1071 paragraphs, matching Geneva), and the sections API delivers precisely-computed verse-marker masking (1071 width-1/2 intervals, no under-masking). But three real defects undercut usefulness: (1) the collection-level Corpus analysis — the whole point of the 6-way validation set — is unreachable from the landing launchpad; (2) TextHiC is a hard dead-end for any text lacking a precomputed self-similarity signal, with no run CTA; and (3) despite masking being enabled by default and the data being correct, the Reading view silently shows verse numbers as unmasked plain text because it never loads the verse store. Near-identical raw-slug member labels further make the 6 subtexts hard to disambiguate in Corpus/Compare.
strengths: Verse-paragraphing fix verified end-to-end: 11-browser.png header shows KJV Matthew '24,754 words · 1071 paragraphs' (was ~131 chapter-level) and the Browser 'Content' track renders 1071 discrete green verse segments across the full 128,450-char width — the fix holds and propagates to the structure view.

Verse-number masking data is methodologically correct: /api/projects/{kjv-matthew}/sections returns 1071 masked_intervals precisely covering verse digits ([0,1]='1', [767,769]='10', [2633,2635]='25'), with zero under-masking of multi-digit verse numbers — the masking engine is accurate.

Reading navigation is genuinely rich and functional: NavigationToolbar.tsx:6-58 offers prev/next paragraph, a three-way coordinate selector (¶ paragraph / chr offset / § section) with live position readout, jump-to-position, and paragraph-level zoom; AppLayout.tsx:98-107 adds CoordinateRuler, TextSearch, SectionNav and TrackPanel — a scholar can navigate the text many ways.

Corpus congruence is correctly computed and surfaced: evidence.json 03-congruence.congruenceCosine shows all_congruent=true, missing=[], all 6 members grouped under a single embedding:cosine key — the cosine-congruent embedding contract for the collection is satisfied and honestly reported ('congruent · cosine' badge).

The TextHiC heatmap component (DotplotView) is a serious, honest visualization when data exists: double-buffered matrix/overlay canvas, role=img with an accessible aria-label reporting live hovered chunk indices and similarity value (DotplotView.tsx:972-973), palette/threshold/PNG/SVG export controls, and wheel-zoom/drag-pan — not a stub.

findings.title: Collection-level Corpus analysis is unreachable from the landing launchpad
findings.evidence: browser/src/components/common/ProjectPicker.tsx:295-302 (TOOLS array lists reading/browser/texthic/characters/analysis/compare — no 'corpus'); openCollection() at :595 only sets the library filter; grep for setActiveTab('corpus') on member-open returns nothing. findings.verify_reasoning:
All three cited facts verified in code and evidence.

(1) TOOLS launchpad omits corpus: ProjectPicker.tsx:295-302 defines exactly 6 tiles (reading/browser/texthic/characters/analysis/compare) — no 'corpus' entry. launchTool()/handleSelect() (lines 630-637, 602-609) only apply a pendingTab drawn from TOOLS, so a user can never pre-select the Corpus tab from Home. Confirmed visually: screenshot 01-landing.png shows the "Analysis tools" row, and evidence.json view "01-landing" heading list ends at "Analysis tools" with no Corpus among the buttons (grep on buttons array: 'Corpus' = False).

(2) openCollection is a dead-end for the overview: ProjectPicker.tsx:595-599 only setActiveCollection + setPage('library') + clears pendingTab. I read the full library-page render (lines 773-830) when a collection is active — it shows filtered BookCover tiles only; there is NO "Open collection overview"/Corpus/pangenome CTA. Clicking a member (line 820, handleSelect(p.id) with default tab) opens Reading, never corpus.

(3) Corpus exists only in-app: TabBar.tsx:11 (Corpus, Alt+7), AppLayout.tsx:127 renders <CorpusView/> only when a project is loaded (landing gate AppLayout.tsx:60-62 returns ProjectPicker when no metadata). grep for setActiveTab('corpus') on member-open returns nothing (CorpusView's own setActiveTab calls go to 'browser'/'compare', lines 350/357). Alt+7 (keyboard.ts:118-122) only works after a text is open, so it does not aid landing-page discoverability.

The hidden feature is genuinely valuable, not a stub: screenshot 02-02-corpus-overview.png renders Block Map, All-Pairs Shared Components matrix, and Phyletic Tree with real data for the 6-way collection — exactly the headline validation feature. So a scholar viewing the "Matthew-Mark 6-Way Cross-Translation Validation (6)" collection sees only book covers, with no signpost that the pangenome/block-map/phyletic-tree exists; they must open an arbitrary member, notice a 7th tab, click it, and re-select the collection in a second dropdown (CorpusView.tsx:372-380).

Severity adjustment (high -> medium): the title word "unreachable" is slightly overstated. The Corpus feature is fully functional and reachable via a persistent, always-visible 7th tab (TabBar.tsx:11) plus Alt+7 once any text is open — it is not broken output and not a broken core flow (the auditor's own bar for "high"). The genuine defect is a discoverability/onboarding gap: the launchpad omits corpus and the collection view provides no route to the overview. Both cited code facts are true; the recommendation (add a Corpus launchpad tile; make the collection view offer "Open collection overview") is sound and worth doing, but this is a notable UX gap, not wrong/misleading data. Note for the fix: CorpusView already has its own collection <select>, so the fix need only route into the corpus tab — it does not require opening a specific member of the target collection.

findings.title: TextHiC is a dead-end empty-state with no call-to-action to run the analysis
findings.evidence: Screenshot 09-texthic.png: centered red text 'Self-similarity matrix not available. Run analysis first.' with inert toolbar (palette dropdown, Fit/Filters/Tracks/PNG/SVG) above and nothing else. Code: DotplotView.tsx:324-327 sets the plain error string on fetch failure; rendered at :945 as static text. evidence.json 09-texthic flags runFirst=true, svg/canvas/rows all 0.

findings.verify_reasoning:
Every factual claim in the finding is verified against code, live API, and the screenshot; only the severity and one recommendation detail are overstated. CODE: DotplotView.tsx:325 sets the plain string `setError('Self-similarity matrix not available. Run analysis first.')` in the fetch `.catch` (lines 324-327). It is rendered at DotplotView.tsx:945 as `{error &&
{error}
}` — a static, centered red string with zero interactive children (no button, link, or onClick). The matrix/tracks block (947-1009) is gated behind `!error && signal`, so nothing else renders. Confirmed: no CTA exists. SCREENSHOT (09-texthic.png): I viewed it. It shows exactly the described layout — the toolbar (Blues palette dropdown, +/- zoom, 100%, Fit, Filters, Tracks, PNG, SVG) sits above an otherwise blank canvas with centered red "Self-similarity matrix not available. Run analysis first." The toolbar buttons act on a matrix that doesn't exist (inert in this state). EVIDENCE.JSON (view "09-texthic", lines 1467-1513): svg=0, canvas=0, rows=0, imgRole=0, sliders=0; flags {error:false, empty:false, runFirst:true, loading:false}; buttons list is the 7 nav tabs + toolbar only. Matches the finding's "runFirst=true, svg/canvas/rows all 0" verbatim. LIVE API: GET /api/projects//self_similarity → HTTP 404 {"detail":"Not Found"}; cs/10/cosine → HTTP 404. So this is a genuinely reachable state for an un-analyzed member (Geneva Mark), not a load bug — the analysis truly has not been run. The dead-end is real for any scholar who opens TextHiC on a text lacking a self-similarity run. FEASIBILITY of the fix (supports the recommendation): viewStore.ts:64-67 exposes setActiveTab('analysis'); DotplotView already consumes the store, so a "Go to Analysis" CTA is trivially wireable. The component ALREADY uses this exact "point the user to the Analysis panel" language at DotplotView.tsx:843-844 ("not cached — produce in Analysis panel"), so the empty-state is simply inconsistent with the component's own established UX pattern — a fair, non-generic critique. WHERE THE FINDING OVERSTATES: (1) Severity. The rubric reserves "high" for wrong/misleading output or a broken core flow. This message is HONEST (correctly states no matrix exists) and the core flow works once analysis is run — it is a UX dead-end / missing-CTA gap, i.e. medium, not high. No data is fabricated or mislabeled; nothing crashes. (2) The alternative recommendation "(or triggers the compute) for the active text" is inaccurate. AnalysisPanel.tsx:879-889 documents that self_similarity "has no runnable defaults — it requires an explicit input bundle"; the panel exposes a "Configure…" layer-picker, not a one-click run. So a bare "Run self-similarity" button firing the compute would 400. The correct CTA is navigation to the Analysis tab (the finding's primary suggestion), which is valid. Net: the problem is real and precisely described; the recommendation's primary path is sound; the "trigger compute" alternative is technically wrong; and high is one notch too hot for an honest empty-state whose only defect is a missing navigation affordance.

dimensions.title: Cross-cutting visualization integrity
dimensions.summary: Palimpsest's charts render REAL data faithfully in the load-bearing cases: the Compare dotplot for Geneva-Mt vs KJV-Mt shows a genuine main diagonal (verified backend matrix main-diag mean 0.741 vs anti-diag 0.066, diagonal is row-argmax for 99.81% of rows), the Edition Diff correctly pairs 1071 vs 1071 verse-paragraphs proving the KJV verse-paragraph fix holds, the phyletic tree encodes the correct topology (Douay-Rheims Vulgate outgroup as root, Geneva-Mark and KJV-Mark at distance 0.0), and the corpus graph classifies 1 core / 1 shell / 6 singleton with DR fragmenting into 7 nodes as ground truth predicts. The integrity problems are in the ENCODING LAYER, not the data: missing legends, a metric-label mismatch on the dotplot, unreadable/overlapping full-id labels in the phyletic tree, and axis-less scatter/legends. No chart was found to fabricate or distort the underlying numbers, but several present them without the scale/units a scholar needs to trust them.
strengths: Compare dotplot is coordinate-honest and data-faithful: I fetched the served matrix (/api/alignment/.../matrix.bin, 1071x1071 float32) and confirmed the visible diagonal is the MAIN diagonal (main-diag mean 0.741 vs anti-diag 0.0659; diagonal is the row-argmax for 99.81% of rows), matching the ground-truth expectation that near-identical same-versification Geneva<->KJV align as one clean full-length diagonal (07-compare-dotplot.png).

Edition Diff (07-compare-diff.png) is the standout view: it correctly aligns Geneva-Mt ¶N <-> KJV-Mt ¶N verse-by-verse (1071 vs 1071), reports '1071 changed / 0 added / 0 removed', and the side-by-side highlighting surfaces genuine translation variants (Judah/Judas, Perez/Phares, Ram/Aram) — direct visual proof the verse-paragraph regeneration fix holds.

Phyletic tree is methodologically correct: /api/collections/matthew-mark-6way/phyletic-tree returns Douay-Rheims-Matthew as the (Vulgate outgroup) root, and Geneva-Mark<->KJV-Mark distance = 0.0 with both attaching to the same internal node at branch_length 0.0 — exactly the signal the collection is designed to exercise.

corpusOverview backend/graph is honest and non-fabricating: /api/collections/matthew-mark-6way/corpus-graph returns 16 nodes / 8 components / classes {singleton:6, shell:1, core:1}, with DR-Mt fragmenting into 7 nodes vs Geneva-Mk/KJV-Mk 1 node each, faithfully rendered as the fragmented-vs-solid block-map lanes in 02-02-corpus-overview.png.

Backend embedding analytics (vectorstore/analytics.py) is rigorously deterministic and self-documenting: PCA sign-canonicalisation (_canonicalize_signs, line 52-60), seeded k-means++ (line 85-135), fixed cosine-distance histogram range [0,2] with explicit float-error clipping to prevent silent undercounts (line 212-216), and index-order preservation documented as the safety contract (module docstring).

findings.verify_reasoning:

dimensions.title: UX & end-to-end workflow completeness
dimensions.summary: Palimpsest is a mature, capable scholarly tool: the landing page surfaces texts and tools clearly with friendly names, the Analysis Suite exposes a "Compute All (17)" batch plus per-track Compute CTAs, the TextHiC/Dotplot heatmap is genuinely explorable (wheel-zoom, drag-pan, click-two-corners region selection with side-by-side text panels, threshold/chunk/metric controls), and costed corpus operations are guarded by an honest pre-run CostDialog. However, the two flagship cross-text journeys — Compare and the Corpus workbench — have real completeness gaps: the Compare tab stacks a "Ready to align" call-to-action ON TOP of already-rendered Dotplot/Diff results (contradictory), Circos and Synteny are hard dead-ends without a manual Align run, the Diff view silently ignores the selected method and reports 1071/1071 "changed" for near-identical Geneva↔KJV, and TextHiC's empty state says "Run analysis first" with no button to do so. Worst for this specific scholarly collection: every Corpus workbench surface labels the 6 members with truncated raw ID slugs so a scholar literally cannot tell Matthew from Mark or DR from Geneva from KJV, and the collection's headline analysis is buried 3-4 clicks behind a single-text detour.
strengths: TextHiC/Dotplot self-similarity heatmap is genuinely interactive, not a static snapshot: wheel-zoom, Ctrl/right-drag pan, click-two-corners region-select that pops side-by-side source-text panels, live hover similarity readout, threshold/diagonal/chapter/chunk-size/metric filters, and an alignments list with click-to-view drill-in (DotplotView.tsx:615-698, 633-675, 876-942; honest 0..1 similarity legend at 796-812).

Analysis Suite has strong discoverability and honest run-state: Tracks sub-tab shows a top-level 'Compute All (17)' plus per-track Compute/Re-run/Details with Type/Evidence/Dependencies columns, and Explore shows computed layers with real metadata ('2 computed · 17 pending', chunking 237 units 99.7985% cov, embedding Qwen3-4bit d2560) rendered as real track strips (08-analysis-tracks.png, 08-analysis-explore.png).

Costed operations are guarded by a reusable pre-run CostDialog that explicitly 'NEVER auto-runs' and explains cost — e.g. the embedding-space reconcile flow lists missing members and warns reconciliation is an expensive per-member run (CostDialog.tsx:5-7, CorpusView.tsx:480-506).

Methodological honesty in encodings: the Corpus 'Spread across the corpus' panel carries the disclaimer 'reference-free graph: this is passage spread across members, not a directional influence/derivation claim', the pangenome badge reports '1 core · 1 shell · 6 singleton' matching ground truth, the phyletic-tree Root selector correctly suggests the DR (Vulgate) outgroup, and the Dotplot renders a clean full-length diagonal for Geneva↔KJV as expected (02-02-corpus-overview.png, 02-06-corpus-analyses.png, 07-compare-dotplot.png).

Landing page is welcoming and legible: friendly display names ('1599 Geneva -- Matthew', 'King James -- Mark'), color-coded covers, word counts, collections in the sidebar, and analysis tools surfaced as cards with descriptions (01-landing.png, evidence.json 01-landing).

dimensions.title: Validation-collection methodology & scientific soundness
dimensions.summary: The matthew-mark-6way collection is a well-designed validation SUBSTRATE with a rigorous, provenance-cited pericope oracle, and the pairwise engine genuinely recovers the headline ground-truth signal (sister translations Geneva↔KJV align as one clean full-length diagonal; Douay-Rheims fragments at Vulgate-versification drift points — verified in records and the dotplot screenshot). However, it does NOT yet function as a scientifically sound validation HARNESS: (1) the 101-pericope / 51-unique synoptic oracle is never loaded or scored by any code — no TP/TN precision/recall is ever computed, so "validation" is eyeball-only; (2) the corpus-graph and phyletic tree built from the word method are degenerate — weak spurious cross-book Jaccard edges transitively union all six members into one giant homology core, collapsing the pangenome and producing a distance matrix/tree that CONTRADICTS ground truth (KJV-Matthew reads as closer to the Mark cluster than to its own sister Matthews); (3) the 6-way collection (the KJV third translation, the piece that makes sister-vs-outgroup testable) has no committed reproducible builder/manifest/validator — it exists only via gitignored .scratch scripts, unlike the 2-member matthew-mark-validation the fixture actually covers. Verse-number masking and embedding congruence are correctly handled (no residue confound; all six cosine-congruent).
strengths: Sister-translation vs Vulgate-outgroup signal is correctly recovered at the pairwise tier: GV-Mt<->KJV-Mt is a single full-length diagonal record q[15:1071]<->t[15:1071] id=0.746 score=519, GV-Mk<->KJV-Mk one diagonal id=0.706, while DR-Mt<->KJV-Mt fragments into 6 records with a gap at the drift point (para 1056-1059) — exactly the ground-truth prediction (alignment.jsonl records; 07-compare-dotplot.png shows a clean sharp diagonal for the sister pair).

The synoptic ground-truth oracle is scholarly and honestly sourced: 101 shared pericopes + 41 Matthew-unique + 10 Mark-unique, cross-verified against Aland's Synopsis and Carlson's Parallel Table, with explicit confidence flags and boundary-reconciliation notes (synoptic-ground-truth.json:5-19, synoptic-ground-truth.md:58-69) — a defensible TP/TN specification even though it is not yet exercised.

Verse-number masking is clean across all three translations with no residue confound: KJV-Mt, GV-Mt, DR-Mt all have verses.jsonl tracks (1071/1071/1070 records) and analyzable_text begins 'The book of the generation...' with masked_delta 1890/4032/6965 and zero leaked verse numbers (verified via Project.analyzable_text), so the recent verse-paragraphing fix holds (paras==verses per member).

Embedding congruence is correct and fail-loud: all 6 members share cosine key embedding:cosine:c9757c16f8473ef1, all_congruent=true, missing=[] (GET /api/collections/matthew-mark-6way/congruence), and the UI badge renders green 'congruent · cosine' (02-02-corpus-overview.png).

The Analyses panel surfaces genuinely correct scholarly signal with honest framing: 991/3185 vocab terms flagged as cross-member boilerplate, most-discriminative terms are translation-specific spellings (Geneva/KJV 'abijah' vs DR 'abia'), and the non-directional caveat is rendered verbatim ('this is passage spread across members, not a directional influence/derivation claim') (02-06-corpus-analyses.png).

findings.title: The synoptic TP/TN oracle is never used to compute precision/recall — validation is eyeball-only
findings.evidence: grep for 'synoptic-ground-truth|shared_pericopes|matthew_unique|mark_unique' across core/, browser/, scripts/, .scratch/*.py returns zero hits outside the fixture file itself; .scratch/run_6way_analysis.py only prints a record-count matrix, never loads the oracle.
findings.recommendation: Implement a scoring harness that loads synoptic-ground-truth.json, maps its chapter:verse pericope ranges to paragraph indices via each member's verses.jsonl, and computes shared-pericope recall (off-diagonal Mt<->Mk records that hit a TP pair) and precision against the 51 unique passages (TN set). Commit it as a test with a documented threshold so the collection actually *validates* the platform rather than merely providing data for it.
findings.verify_reasoning:
Every claim in the finding checks out against the code, the live API, and the fixtures.

1. Oracle exists and is usable. core/tests/fixtures/validation-mm/synoptic-ground-truth.json is a complete, structured TP/TN dataset: 101 shared_pericopes (TP) each with matthew + mark chapter:verse ranges (e.g. "3:1-6"/"1:2-6", tradition, confidence), plus 41 matthew_unique + 10 mark_unique = 51 TN passages. Its companion .md (lines 11-21, 43-56) explicitly documents the intended TP/TN precision/recall scoring and the failure modes it should catch. So the premise that a mappable oracle exists is true.

2. Grep confirms zero consumption. grep for shared_pericopes|matthew_unique|mark_unique across all *.py (excluding the fixture dir itself) returns nothing. The only Python files matching 'synoptic'/'recall'/'ground-truth' are incidental: .scratch/build_report.py mentions 'recall' only re a *different* cosine-based estimated_recall tautology (not the oracle); .scratch/audit6/analyze_comparisons.py:39 has 'synoptic' only inside a hard-coded label string "CROSS-BOOK (Mt<->Mk synoptic) EXPECT weak off-diag"; core/tests/test_collections.py:70 uses 'synoptic' only as a create_collection description arg. None load the oracle.

3. run_6way_analysis.py is exactly as described. Its report() (lines 75-88) prints an upper-triangle record-count matrix; align() (46-54) writes per-pair records + top_score. It never opens synoptic-ground-truth.json and computes no metric.

4. Validation is genuinely eyeball-only. The fixture's own validate.py performs only string-presence/leakage checks (lines 32-56), no scoring. analyze_comparisons.py buckets pairs by hard-coded book/translation labels into "EXPECT weak off-diag" categories and prints record counts (lines 42-50) — the accept/reject judgment is left to a human reading the printed matrix. There is no test with a documented threshold that scores off-diagonal Mt↔Mk recall against the TP set or precision against the 51 TN passages.

5. Live substrate confirmed. GET http://localhost:8092/api/collections returns matthew-mark-6way with the 6 expected members (DR/Geneva/KJV × Matt/Mark), matching the setup; no scoring endpoint consumes the oracle.

Severity: the recommendation (build a harness that maps pericope ranges → paragraph indices via each member's verses.jsonl and computes shared-pericope recall + TN precision, committed as a thresholded test) is well-founded and directly addresses the gap. This is a real scientific-soundness deficiency for a dimension defined as "validation-collection methodology" — the collection provides data to the platform but does not actually *validate* it against ground truth, so the platform's core cross-text-detection claim is unmeasured. It is validation-tooling incompleteness rather than a live production defect (no user-facing wrong output), which places it at the high/medium boundary; I keep it at high because the dimension is specifically about validation soundness and a fully-built oracle sitting unused is the sharpest possible instance of that gap.

findings.title: Word-method corpus graph over-merges all six members into one giant core via spurious cross-book edges — pangenome is degenerate
findings.evidence: GET /api/collections/matthew-mark-6way/corpus-graph: core component c7 unions all 6 members (n1 DR-Mt whole book <-> n7 DR-Mk whole book via 10 edges score 0.16-1.13; n5 GV-Mt <-> n8 GV-Mk 18 edges score 0.22-1.72). Only 16 nodes total; each book is one giant anchor (n1 = DR-Mt paras[15:1056]). Raw Jaccard on .lower().split() (cross_similarity.py:113-128, no stopword strip) lets shared function words push cross-book similarity above smith_waterman's score=sim*2-1 floor (smith_waterman.py:74), and uf.union (corpus_graph.py:292) transitively merges everything.
findings.recommendation: Gate homology-union edges by a score/cross-similarity threshold (not just anchor_trim block-boundary trimming, which is 0.0 here and cannot remove whole spurious edges), or stopword-strip the word-overlap metric so cross-book function-word Jaccard drops below the SW floor. Otherwise the pangenome/tree tier is uninterpretable on real text despite green synthetic unit tests.
findings.verify_reasoning: STRUCTURAL SYMPTOM CONFIRMED (verified live + on disk). GET /api/collections/matthew-mark-6way/corpus-graph: summary shows core=1, shell=1, singleton=6, n_nodes=16, n_edges=172, anchor_trim=0.0 — all exactly as the finding states. Component c7 is classified "core" and unions members [0,1,2,3,4,5] via nodes n1,n2,n3 (DR-Mt),n5(GV-Mt),n6(KJV-Mt),n7(DR-Mk),n8(GV-Mk),n9(KJV-Mk). Cited edge data matches to the number: n1<->n7 = 10 edges score 0.158..1.127; n5<->n8 = 18 edges score 0.222..1.716 (also n6<->n9 = 14 edges 0.167..1.649). 66 of 172 edges are cross-book Matt<->Mark. Each book is one giant whole-book anchor (n1=DR-Mt para[15:1056]=1041 paras; n7=DR-Mk para[0:676]; etc.), built by _merge_intervals collapsing 56 of 61 scattered DR-Mt intervals into one span. COUNTERFACTUAL PROVES CAUSATION: I ran union-find with the 66 cross-book edges removed — the graph cleanly splits into a Matthew cluster (m0,m1,m2) and a Mark cluster (m3,m4,m5), the biologically-correct pangenome. So the cross-book edges are indeed what collapse everything into one core. The pangenome core is degenerate and the tree loses the Matt/Mark split (phyletic-tree distances put GV-Mk=KJV-Mk at 0.0 and cannot express a Matthew-vs-Mark clade). CODE PATH CONFIRMED: comparisons use method="word" (compute_word_overlap, cross_similarity.py:108-130, set(t.lower().split()) no stopword strip); server.py:2751 calls smith_waterman with default score_threshold=0.0; smith_waterman.py:74 maps sim->2*sim-1 (floor at sim=0.5); corpus_graph.py:292 uf.union with no score gate. MECHANISM AND FIX REFUTED. The finding blames "shared function words pushing cross-book Jaccard above the SW floor" and recommends stopword-stripping. This is factually wrong. I read the actual paragraph text behind the cross-book edges: the highest-scoring (Mt 26:31-32 <-> Mk 14:27-28, "I will strike the shepherd and the sheep shall be dispersed"), the lowest-scoring (Mt 26:28 <-> Mk 14:24, "this is my blood of the new testament"), and a mid edge (Mt 9:10 <-> Mk 2:15, "publicans and sinners... sat down with Jesus") are all GENUINE verbatim synoptic Gospel parallels within the same translation — real content homology, not function-word noise. I computed no-stopword Jaccard on these pairs: 0.60, 0.50, 0.73 — still at or above the 0.5 floor, i.e. stopword stripping does NOT remove them because the overlap is content words (Jesus, blood, testament, shepherd, sheep, publicans, sinners, disciples). The recommended remediation would therefore fail. The true root cause is whole-book anchoring: _merge_intervals (corpus_graph.py:267) collapses every member into a single book-spanning anchor, so a single genuine shared pericope (legitimately shell-level homology) drags the entire book into the same union-find component. The honest fix is passage-level anchoring / not merging disjoint pericope intervals into one whole-book node (and/or a min-component-support gate), not stopword stripping. SEVERITY: the platform-level defect (pangenome/tree tier uninterpretable on real cross-Gospel text despite green synthetic unit tests) is real and worth high attention, but the finding's stated cause and fix are incorrect, so it is partial, not confirmed. I hold severity at high because the symptom is a genuine correctness failure of a headline tier, but a downstream engineer acting only on this finding's recommendation would not fix it.

findings.title: Phyletic tree and distance matrix contradict ground truth — KJV-Matthew clusters with Mark, not with sister Matthews
findings.evidence: GET .../phyletic-tree distance matrix: KJV-Mt<->GV-Mt=0.750 but KJV-Mt<->GV-Mk=0.500 and KJV-Mt<->DR-Mk=0.667, so KJV-Mt is nearer the Mark cluster than its own book; tree topology places KJV-Mt in node2 with node0={GV-Mk,KJV-Mk}. GV-Mk<->KJV-Mk collapse to distance 0.000 (identical participation=1). Ground truth (substrate + synoptic-ground-truth.md) expects a book-first split then translation-within-book, DR rooted as Vulgate outgroup. The all-pairs matrix in 02-02-corpus-overview.png is a near-uniform '1' — no sister/outgroup structure recoverable.
findings.recommendation: This is a downstream symptom of the over-merge finding: phylo.component_distance_matrix (phylo.py:33) is Jaccard over homology components, so a 1-core/degenerate graph yields a meaningless distance matrix. Fix the graph first; then add a test asserting the tree separates Mt from Mk and pairs Geneva<->KJV within book before this collection can be cited as validating the phyletic tier.
findings.verify_reasoning: Verified by direct grounding on all three vectors. (1) API: GET http://localhost:8092/api/collections/matthew-mark-6way/phyletic-tree returns the exact distances claimed — with member order [DR-Mt, GV-Mt, KJV-Mt, DR-Mk, GV-Mk, KJV-Mk], D[KJV-Mt][GV-Mt]=0.75, D[KJV-Mt][GV-Mk]=0.5, D[KJV-Mt][DR-Mk]=0.666667, D[GV-Mk][KJV-Mk]=0.0. I independently recomputed the full matrix from the captured graph's component memberships (.scratch/audit6/_graph.json) and it matches to the digit. (2) Tree topology matches the finding exactly: rooted at DR-Mt, KJV-Mt is under node2 alongside node0={GV-Mk,KJV-Mk}; i.e. KJV-Matthew's nearest cluster is Mark, not the other Matthews, and GV-Mk/KJV-Mk collapse (branch_length 0.0, distance 0.0). (3) Screenshot 02-02-corpus-overview.png shows the '1 core / 1 shell / 6 singleton' badge and a near-uniform all-pairs '1' grid (single '2' at DR-Mt<->GV-Mt) with no recoverable sister/outgroup structure — the phyletic tree pane shows no clean book-first split. Ground truth (core/tests/fixtures/validation-mm/synoptic-ground-truth.md + collection design) expects Geneva/KJV as near-identical sisters and DR as Vulgate outgroup, book-first — not recovered. ATTRIBUTION VERIFIED CORRECT: root cause is the over-merged graph, component c7 (classification 'core') contains all 6 members, so the Jaccard-over-components distance in phylo.component_distance_matrix (phylo.py:33) is driven almost entirely by which members appear in extra singleton/shell components. GV-Mk and KJV-Mk each participate in ONLY c7 (participation=1), so they are indistinguishable and collapse to 0.0 — not because the texts are identical but because the graph gives them identical component profiles. phylo.py math is correct and unit-tested (test_phylo.py::test_jaccard_distance_matrix confirms the formula; its own {0,1,2,3}-core fixture reproduces the same degeneracy), so the defect is genuinely upstream in graph construction, exactly as the finding's CLAIM states ('downstream symptom of the over-merge finding; fix the graph first'). RECOMMENDATION VALID AND UNIMPLEMENTED: existing tests (test_corpus_graph.py::test_phyletic_tree_distances_and_root, :247 reroot) assert only mechanical properties (formula, deterministic root, leaves present); no test asserts the tree separates Mt from Mk or pairs Geneva<->KJV within book on real data, so the collection cannot yet be cited as validating the phyletic tier. Minor calibration: the matrix is not literally 'meaningless' — a faint-but-correct signal survives (the DR-Mt<->GV-Mt '2' cell, the participation gradient DR-Mt=5>GV-Mt=3>KJV-Mt=2), and phylo.py:397 frames the tree in-code as a 'reading… not stored ground truth', so severity stays HIGH rather than critical (read-only, no data corruption, honesty-framed) but above medium (flagship phylogenetic output of a validation collection actively contradicts its own ground truth with no guard test).

findings.title: The 6-way collection has no committed reproducible builder, manifest, or validator — only gitignored .scratch scripts
findings.evidence: core/tests/fixtures/validation-mm/{build.py:48 CID='matthew-mark-validation', manifest.json:1, validate.py:8-10} all cover only the 2-member Douay/Geneva collection. The KJV member and the 6-way split are built by .scratch/run_6way_analysis.py, .scratch/embed_6way.py, .scratch/split_mm_ids.json (all gitignored). README.md never mentions KJV or six members.
findings.recommendation: Promote the 6-way build to the committed fixture: add KJV ingest/layout/verse-mask steps to build.py, a 6-member manifest.json with expected char/word/verse counts and reference-sha prefixes, and extend validate.py to assert all six. Without this the standing validation substrate is not reproducible from the repo — a provenance failure for a scientific harness.
findings.verify_reasoning: Every factual claim verified. (1) Committed fixture core/tests/fixtures/validation-mm/ covers ONLY the 2-member collection: build.py line 48 CID='matthew-mark-validation'; manifest.json has 2 members (DR-MM, Geneva-MM) with collection_id 'matthew-mark-validation'; validate.py validates only the Geneva-MM member. Grep of both git HEAD and working-tree build.py/validate.py/README.md for kjv/king james/6way/six/matthew-mark-6way returns nothing. (2) The KJV member and 6-way split are produced by gitignored scratch scripts: .scratch/build_kjv_mm.py (its own docstring: 'Build the KJV Matthew+Mark subtext (3rd translation for the 6-text collection)'), .scratch/embed_6way.py, .scratch/split_mm_ids.json, .scratch/run_6way_analysis.py — all confirmed to exist and all gitignored (git check-ignore -> .gitignore:57 '.scratch/'); git ls-files shows no tracked 6way/kjv files. (3) README makes no mention of KJV or six members. (4) Live GET http://localhost:8092/api/collections confirms matthew-mark-6way exists with 6 members (DR/Geneva/KJV x Matt/Mark), it is the audit focus, the read-only server runs on the gitignored .scratch/validation-mm workspace, and 6 split member dirs exist on disk. So the 6-way — the very collection the audit substrate designates as focus — is not reproducible from the repo. The recommendation (promote 6-way to committed build.py/manifest.json/validate.py with KJV steps + 6-member expected counts + sha prefixes) is correct and actionable. Severity adjusted high->medium for fairness: the finding itself acknowledges the 2-member DR/Geneva collection IS fully and reproducibly committed (builder with idempotent embed step, manifest with reference_sha256 prefixes + expected char/word/verse counts, validator). That 2-way is the canonical 'standing validation collection' per committed README/build.py and remains sound. The 6-way is a very recent extension (its .scratch builders dated Jul 1, same day) that has not yet been promoted to a committed fixture — a real reproducibility gap for the 6-way, but 'committed fixture lags the live analysis' rather than 'the validation harness has no reproducible provenance at all.' The load-bearing committed substrate does not silently rot; the gap is a pending-promotion delta, which fits medium.

findings.title: Record-count is used as a similarity proxy but conflates translation-identity with versification-identity (Goodhart risk)
findings.evidence: 6-way pairwise tally: SISTER same-versification pairs (GV-Mt<->KJV-Mt, GV-Mk<->KJV-Mk) yield 1 record each (one giant diagonal), while DR different-versification pairs yield 39-58 records (fragmented). CROSS-BOOK synoptic pairs yield 0-18 records driven by function-word noise (GV-Mt<->DR-Mk=0, DR-Mt<->GV-Mk=3, GV-Mt<->GV-Mk=18). A naive 'more records = more similar' or 'fewer = more similar' reading is wrong in both directions.
findings.recommendation: Never surface raw record count as a similarity signal in the overview/matrix; use coverage (fraction of paragraphs aligned) and mean identity/score instead. The giant-diagonal-vs-fragment asymmetry means the fragmentation count measures versification alignment, not textual similarity — document this explicitly so users don't misread the all-pairs matrix.

findings.title: Sweep reports null run-level recall despite measured per-pair recall — undermines the touted honesty guarantee
findings.evidence: GET .../sweeps roll-up shows estimated_recall=None for run 8a555cc5f398 (mode=high-recall, word_overlap), yet GET .../sweep/{run_id} per-pair entries all carry measured recall 0.012-0.236 with sample sizes 255-402. The C6c/C7b journal claims recall is reported empirically or 'n/a', but here real measurements exist while the headline reads unmeasured.
findings.recommendation: Aggregate the per-pair estimated_recall (sample-weighted mean) into the run-level roll-up in list_sweep_runs so the manager shows the true ~0.09 mean recall rather than n/a. A user seeing n/a would wrongly conclude no recall was measured, when in fact the low value is the key honest signal (word-LSH recovers ~9% of translation similarity at verse granularity).

findings.title: Cross-book synoptic detection is at the noise floor — symmetric pairs disagree (0 vs 3 records)
findings.evidence: GV-Mt<->DR-Mk produced 0 alignment records on disk (cmp-2a1a8e996d2523a5, reported in corpus-graph summary.pairs_missing), while the comparable cross-book DR-Mt<->GV-Mk produced 3 and DR-Mt<->KJV-Mk produced 3. The synoptic true-positive off-diagonal signal (101 shared pericopes) is essentially undetected by the word method — the C6a journal itself flags '3 cross-book records' vs 100 diagonal.
findings.recommendation: For the synoptic (off-diagonal) validation claim, score the embedding-method alignments, not word-overlap — the members are already cosine-congruent. Word-overlap should be documented as validating only translation-equivalence (the diagonal), and the synoptic recall claim must be evaluated on embeddings, else the collection cannot validate the cross-content detection it was built to exercise.

findings.title: Green synthetic unit tests mask the real-text degeneracy — fixture over-fits the happy path
findings.evidence: tests/test_corpus_graph.py + test_phylo.py = 20 passed, but they use hand-written clean book-separated comparison dirs that prove '1 core / 1 shell / 3 singleton' by construction and never inject the spurious weak cross-book edges real scripture produces. This is the exact 'unit tests with on-disk fixtures missed both [live bugs]' pattern the C2 journal (collections-tier-build-journal.md:85) already documented.
findings.recommendation: Add a regression test that builds the corpus graph from the actual 6-way (or a small real-text fixture with genuine function-word overlap) and asserts the pangenome does NOT collapse to a single core and the tree separates books — a live-data test alongside the synthetic ones, so the over-merge cannot silently reappear.

findings.title: Summary counts match stated ground truth (1 core/1 shell/6 singleton) while the underlying structure is wrong — a right-answer-for-wrong-reasons trap
findings.evidence: GET .../corpus-graph summary reports core:1, shell:1, singleton:6 — numerically identical to the substrate's stated pangenome expectation, and rendered as such in 02-02-corpus-overview.png. But the single core is the degenerate all-members giant merge (finding above), not six clean per-book/translation homologies, so the matching headline is coincidental.
findings.recommendation: Do not treat the core/shell/singleton headline as passing validation. The pangenome check must assert component *composition* (which members, spanning which books) against the oracle, not just the three counts — otherwise a degenerate graph passes the eyeball test.
